Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the MA contract-year audited financial statement package and its HPMS upload; CFO attests, Chief Audit Executive runs the external auditor relationship

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.516(a) and (d) (financial reporting and audited statements) re-read on eCFR at audit planning, plus the current-year CMS HPMS financial reporting memo, and 42 CFR 422.590(f)/422.592 for the IRE auto-forward volumes disclosed in the claims-liability note

In-scope processes.value: Year-end close for every MA contract (H-number) and its licensed legal entity, external audit fieldwork, CFO attestation, and the HPMS Annual Audited Financial Statement upload including the administrative-cost, net-worth and related-party schedules

In-scope systems.value: Contract-level trial balance and audit adjustment postings in the GL; consolidation in the close tool; the signed audit report and HPMS confirmation filed in the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: MA Audited Financial Statement Procedure — audit timetable, PBC list, H-number to legal-entity mapping, CMS schedule preparation, HPMS Contract Financial Information upload steps, and the claims-liability note support

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and accepted by the Audit Committee; re-approved each January when CMS publishes the annual financial reporting HPMS memo

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — audited financial statements due to CMS within 180 days of fiscal-year end (30 June for a calendar-year contract); unaudited annual statements within 120 days; quarterly statements within 60 days of quarter end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts to the Controller and Regulatory Reporting Manager at day 90, day 45, day 15 and day 5 before the 180-day HPMS due date, plus a fieldwork-start alert 120 days before

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed audit report, opinion, management representation letter, adjustment log, CMS schedules and the HPMS submission confirmation retained 10 years per the 42 CFR 422.504(d) record retention requirement

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A late or rejected HPMS upload, an unposted audit adjustment above performance materiality, or a going-concern/material-weakness finding is logged as a compliance exception with root cause, CMS notification decision and closure date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off the final statements, every post-close adjustment and any resubmission to CMS

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every MA contract (H-number) and licensed entity required to file audited financials for the audit year, plus the full audit adjustment log and every management letter point raised

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a missed, late or rejected HPMS upload; any audit adjustment above performance materiality left unposted, or any CMS schedule that does not tie to the audited statements to the dollar, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once per audit cycle within 30 days of the HPMS upload, with a readiness checkpoint at audit planning (day 120 before the due date)

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must have no role in the close, the schedule preparation or the HPMS upload

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual audited-financials compliance workpaper (population of H-numbers, tie-out, deadline recomputation, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository under contract year and H-number

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Audit report, opinion, CMS schedules, GL tie-out and HPMS confirmation number producible for a CMS financial review or Account Manager request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager owns correspondence with the CMS Account Manager and the Division of Plan Oversight; Regulatory Counsel clears any restatement, going-concern or net-worth deficiency disclosure before it is sent

checklist.step: Lock the reporting entity list for the audit year
actions: Pull the active contract list from HPMS Contract Management and list every H-number in force at any point in the audit year, including contracts non-renewed mid-year.
Map each H-number to the licensed legal entity that carries it and to the state of domicile, and confirm the mapping with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Record the fiscal-year end for each entity and compute its 180-day CMS due date on the entity row.
Save the entity/contract matrix as the cover sheet of the audit binder in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: every in-force H-number is mapped to a legal entity, fiscal-year end and computed CMS due date on one signed matrix.

checklist.step: Publish the audit timetable and the PBC list
actions: Agree with the external audit engagement partner the planning meeting date, fieldwork window, draft-opinion date and signature date, working backwards from the 180-day CMS due date.

Take the auditor's prepared-by-client list and assign each item an internal owner (Controller, Statutory Reporting Manager, Appointed Actuary, Compliance Manager) and a due date at least 10 business days before fieldwork.
Load the timetable into the close calendar and send it to the CFO, Controller and Audit Committee chair.
Escalate any PBC item without a named owner within 5 business days of publication.
checklist.done: a dated timetable and a fully owned PBC list are issued and the signature date leaves at least 15 days of buffer before the CMS due date.

checklist.step: Confirm the external auditor's independence and engagement terms
actions: Obtain the auditor's written independence confirmation covering the firm, the engagement team and any non-audit services provided to the MA entities.
Compare the non-audit fee schedule to the Audit Committee's pre-approval log and flag any service performed without pre-approval.
Post the engagement letter, independence confirmation and fee schedule to the board portal for the Audit Committee meeting.
Record the Audit Committee's appointment resolution and the meeting date in the minute book.
checklist.done: a current independence confirmation and an Audit Committee appointment resolution are on file before fieldwork starts.

checklist.step: Close the contract-year ledger and produce the trial balance by H-number
actions: Run the year-end close checklist to completion and confirm every balance sheet account is reconciled and signed in the close tool with no unexplained ageing over 90 days.
Produce a trial balance per legal entity with the H-number segment reported separately for premium revenue, medical expense, administrative expense and reinsurance.

Reconcile CMS capitation revenue in the ledger to the monthly membership report (MMR) totals for the twelve payment months and document the difference by cause (retroactivity, risk-adjustment true-up, Part D reconciliation).
Hand the signed trial balance and the MMR reconciliation to the Controller and the audit team.
checklist.done: the trial balance is closed by entity and H-number and capitation revenue ties to the twelve MMRs with every variance explained.

checklist.step: Produce the claims liability support with the Appointed Actuary
actions: Run the IBNR development by contract and service category using paid claims data through the valuation cut-off, and produce the completion-factor and per-member-per-month exhibits.
Reconcile the paid claims triangle to the claims platform paid totals and to the GL medical expense account for the year.
Prepare the prior-year reserve run-off exhibit showing redundancy or deficiency by contract.
Sign the actuarial memorandum supporting the recorded liability and deliver it, with the underlying data extract, to the external auditor and the Controller.
checklist.done: a signed actuarial memorandum, development exhibits and a claims-to-GL reconciliation support the recorded claims liability for every H-number.

checklist.step: Prepare the CMS-specific financial schedules
actions: Build the administrative cost schedule splitting direct medical, quality-improvement activity and non-benefit expense on the same basis used for the MLR report.
Compute the net worth position for each entity against the CMS fiscal soundness expectation and against the state minimum capital requirement, and show the cushion in dollars.
Prepare the related-party and intercompany transaction schedule listing management fees, capitation to affiliated providers and cost allocations, each tied to the intercompany agreement.
Tie every schedule line to a trial balance account and attach the tie-out so no CMS schedule figure exists outside the ledger.
checklist.done: administrative cost, net worth and related-party schedules are complete and each line ties to a named trial balance account.

checklist.step: Deliver the PBC package and support fieldwork
actions: Upload each PBC item to the auditor's request portal against its request number, and mark the request closed only when the auditor accepts it.
Log every auditor question with the date received, the responder and the date answered, and chase any item open more than 3 business days.
Route sample selections for premium, claims and administrative expense to the owning team and collect the source documents (MMR page, claim EOB, invoice, contract) for each item.
Report open PBC items daily to the Controller during fieldwork.
checklist.done: every PBC and sample request is answered and accepted by the auditor with a dated response log.

checklist.step: Clear audit adjustments and control deficiencies before the opinion date
actions: Take the auditor's summary of unadjusted and proposed adjustments and record each with its account, amount, contract and side of the balance sheet.
Post every adjustment above performance materiality to the ledger in the audit-year period and re-run the affected reconciliations.
For each passed adjustment, document why it is below materiality individually and in aggregate and obtain CFO agreement in writing.
Log each control deficiency, significant deficiency and material weakness with an owner and a remediation date before the opinion is signed.
checklist.done: no adjustment above performance materiality is unposted and every deficiency has a written owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Assemble the Part C appeals and IRE data used in the disclosures
actions: Extract from the appeals case system the count of reconsiderations affirmed adverse and auto-forwarded to the CMS-contracted Independent Review Entity under 42 CFR 422.590(f), by contract and quarter.
Reconcile that count to the IRE's own case acknowledgement file and explain any difference before it is used.
Give the Controller the volume, the IRE overturn rate and the estimated financial exposure from overturned cases for the contingency and claims-liability disclosures.
Attach the extract and the reconciliation to the audit binder as support for the disclosure.
checklist.done: the IRE auto-forward volumes and overturn exposure used in the disclosures reconcile to the IRE acknowledgement file.

checklist.step: Sign the management representation letter
actions: Read the auditor's draft representation letter line by line and confirm each assertion against the supporting workpaper reference.
Confirm with the General Counsel that the litigation and regulatory-matter representations match the legal letter responses received.
Confirm with the Compliance Officer that no known CMS non-compliance, sanction or enrollment suspension is omitted.
Sign and date the letter no earlier than the opinion date and file the signed original in the audit binder.
checklist.done: a signed, dated representation letter matching the opinion date is in the binder with legal and compliance confirmations behind it.

checklist.step: Take the statements through the Audit Committee for issuance
actions: Post the draft audited statements, the auditor's report and the management letter to the board portal at least 5 business days before the Audit Committee meeting.
Schedule the auditor's private session with the committee without management present and record that it occurred.
Capture the committee's resolution approving issuance, with the date and the members present, in the minutes.
Release the statements for filing only after the resolution is recorded.
checklist.done: an Audit Committee resolution approving issuance is minuted and the private session is recorded.

checklist.step: Upload the audited statements to HPMS
actions: In HPMS open Contract Management, then Contract Financial Information, and select the audited annual financial statement submission for the contract year.
Attach the signed audit report with the opinion, the full financial statements with notes, and the administrative cost, net worth and related-party schedules for each H-number.
Complete the submitter contact fields and the attestation, then submit before the 180-day due date (30 June for a calendar-year contract).
Save the HPMS confirmation page with its submission identifier and timestamp into the financial reporting repository and the internal filing calendar row.
checklist.done: each H-number shows a submitted status in HPMS with a saved confirmation identifier dated on or before the 180-day deadline.

checklist.step: Clear HPMS validation errors and CMS follow-up questions
actions: Check the HPMS submission status the next business day and open any validation or rejection message returned against the upload.
Correct the underlying schedule or attachment, re-upload, and record both the original and the corrected submission identifiers on the calendar row.
Answer CMS Account Manager questions within the date stated in the request, routing financial answers through the Controller and disclosure answers through Regulatory Counsel.
Log every resubmission as an exception in the filing tracker with its cause.
checklist.done: HPMS shows an accepted submission with no open validation errors and every CMS question is answered by its stated date.

checklist.step: Drive the management letter points to closure
actions: Raise one GRC issue per management letter point with the auditor's wording, the process owner and the agreed remediation date.
Require a written control design change for every significant deficiency, not a promise of extra review.
Test each remediation before closing the issue and attach the test evidence to the issue record.
Report open points and their ageing to the Audit Committee each quarter until closed.
checklist.done: every management letter point is an owned GRC issue with tested evidence before closure.

checklist.step: Retain the audit evidence for the CMS retention period
actions: Move the audit binder (statements, opinion, representation letter, adjustment log, CMS schedules, actuarial memorandum, HPMS confirmation) into the compliance evidence repository indexed by contract year and H-number.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d) and set the disposition hold so the record cannot age out early.
Confirm the record is retrievable by H-number, fiscal year and HPMS submission identifier.
Record the retention label and index date on the filing calendar row.
checklist.done: the audit binder is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by H-number and submission identifier.

testing.step: Build the population of contracts required to file audited financials
actions: Extract the HPMS contract list for the audit year, including contracts terminated or non-renewed mid-year, and record each H-number with its legal entity.
Compare the extract to the legal entity register and the state certificate-of-authority list to catch entities that file but carry no active H-number.
Resolve every difference with the Regulatory Reporting Manager before drawing a sample and note the resolution in the workpaper.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and record count.
testing.done: the population reconciles to both the HPMS contract list and the legal entity register with a signed record count.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed statements to the general ledger
actions: Take the audited statements as filed in HPMS and tie total premium revenue, medical expense, administrative expense, total assets and equity to the post-close trial balance for each entity.
Trace any difference to a posted consolidation or reclassification entry and read the entry support.
Reject a reconciliation that relies on a plug line with no journal reference.
Record the tie-out on a single schedule showing filed figure, ledger figure and difference for each caption.
testing.done: every filed caption ties to the ledger or to a referenced consolidation entry, with no unsupported plug.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of H-numbers, since the population is small and each carries its own CMS deadline.
Take 25 audit adjustments selected at random with a recorded seed from the full adjustment log, plus 100% of adjustments above performance materiality.
Take 100% of management letter points.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers every H-number and every adjustment above performance materiality.

testing.step: Re-perform the CMS schedule build for sampled contracts
actions: Rebuild the administrative cost split from the trial balance without looking at the filed schedule, using the documented allocation basis.
Recompute the net worth position and compare the cushion to the state minimum capital requirement and the CMS fiscal soundness expectation.
Compare your figures to the filed schedule and treat any difference over the workpaper tolerance as an exception, including a right answer reached from a wrong allocation basis.
Attach both build files to the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled contract has an independent schedule rebuild with differences quantified and explained.

testing.step: Trace the HPMS submission and its confirmation identifier
actions: In HPMS open Contract Management, then Contract Financial Information, for each sampled H-number and read the submission status, timestamp and identifier.
Compare the identifier and timestamp to the confirmation saved in the financial reporting repository and treat any mismatch as an exception.
Open the attached documents and confirm the opinion is signed, dated and covers the entity that holds the H-number.
Capture the HPMS submission detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled H-number traces to a real HPMS submission whose identifier and attachments match the retained evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the 180-day deadline and measure timeliness
actions: Recompute due date equals fiscal-year end plus 180 days for each entity and compare it to the date recorded on the filing calendar.
Compare the HPMS submission timestamp to the recomputed due date and record days early or days late for each contract.
Where a resubmission occurred, measure timeliness against the accepted submission, not the first attempt.
Treat any submission after the recomputed due date as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every contract shows a recomputed deadline and a measured filing date with no unreported late submission.

testing.step: Test that audit adjustments were posted and deficiencies captured
actions: For each sampled adjustment, trace the journal entry to the ledger with its posting date, period and preparer, and confirm it landed in the audit-year period.
Confirm every passed adjustment appears on the summary of unadjusted differences with a written CFO acceptance.
Confirm each management letter point has a GRC issue with an owner and a remediation date opened within 30 days of the letter.
Flag any adjustment posted only to a reporting overlay and never to the ledger.
testing.done: each sampled adjustment is traced to a posted ledger entry or an accepted passed-adjustment schedule, and every letter point has an owned issue.

testing.step: Test auditor independence and the representation letter
actions: Read the independence confirmation and compare the non-audit services listed to the Audit Committee pre-approval log entry by entry.
Confirm the representation letter is signed, dated no earlier than the opinion date, and covers CMS non-compliance, sanctions and enrollment actions.
Confirm the legal letter responses on file support the litigation representations.
Treat any non-audit service without pre-approval as an exception regardless of fee size.
testing.done: independence is confirmed with no unapproved non-audit service and the representation letter is properly dated and supported.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception naming the H-number, the caption or adjustment affected and the CMS impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (entity list incomplete, schedule allocation basis wrong, close ran late, HPMS upload rejected, adjustment unposted) and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any late or rejected CMS filing, open a self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next audit cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-late-filing and zero-unposted-material-adjustment thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with a workpaper reference behind each supporting statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who had no role in the close, the schedules or the upload, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any breach to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper by contract year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the CMS Part C submission calendar for every H-number; the Compliance Officer owns the compliance-program elements the calendar is derived from

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi) compliance program elements, 42 CFR 422.516 reporting requirements, and 42 CFR 422.137(d)/422.138 utilization management committee and continuity-of-coverage duties, each re-checked on eCFR when the annual Part C Reporting Requirements technical specifications HPMS memo is released

In-scope processes.value: Every recurring CMS Part C submission for each contract: bid and Plan Benefit Package, Part C Reporting Requirements sections, MLR report, MOC and CCIP/QIP submissions, ANOC/EOC mailing, the annual utilization management committee review under 422.137(d), and the compliance program effectiveness cycle

In-scope systems.value: HPMS submission modules drive the calendar rows; each row links to its evidence pack in the compliance evidence repository and to a task in the filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: Part C Regulatory Calendar Procedure — how a calendar row is created from an HPMS memo or CFR citation, who is named preparer/reviewer/submitter, what constitutes timeliness evidence, and the escalation path when a row slips

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Compliance Officer and reviewed by the Compliance Committee each January, and re-opened whenever CMS issues an HPMS memo that adds, removes or re-dates a submission

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous. Fixed anchors: bid by the first Monday in June, MLR report by the last Monday in July, Part C Reporting Requirements annual data by the last Monday in February, ANOC/EOC delivered by 30 September, plus event-driven clocks of 14 calendar days for standard service organization determinations, 30 days for grievances and reconsiderations of payment, and 60 days for reconsideration requests

Deadline reminders configured.value: Automated reminders on every row at T-45, T-21, T-7 and T-1 to the named preparer, with escalation to the Compliance Officer at T-3 if the row is not in Prepared status

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each row retains the submitted file, the HPMS confirmation with its timestamp, the preparer and reviewer sign-offs and the source data extract, held 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any row submitted after its CMS deadline, submitted without reviewer sign-off, or discovered missing from the calendar is logged as a compliance-program exception with root cause and a calendar control change

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Compliance Officer signs off every late or missed submission and every change to the calendar's row inventory

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every calendar row with a CMS due date in the test period across all H-numbers, plus every HPMS memo issued in the period that should have created or changed a row

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a missed CMS deadline; a row that exists but has no retained confirmation is a fail; any HPMS memo obligation absent from the calendar is a fail regardless of whether the underlying submission was made

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's due rows and includes a completeness sweep of every HPMS memo issued in the quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not prepare, review or submit any calendar row in the tested quarter

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly Part C calendar completeness and timeliness workpaper (row population, memo sweep, confirmation trace, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Calendar export showing row, citation, due date, submitted date and HPMS confirmation identifier, producible for a CMS program audit compliance-program request within the 15-business-day universe window

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers CMS Account Manager submission queries; the Compliance Officer owns any program-audit compliance-program element response and Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a missed submission

checklist.step: Rebuild the calendar row inventory from the regulatory source
actions: List every recurring CMS Part C submission from the current Part C Reporting Requirements technical specifications, the annual HPMS reporting memo and 42 CFR 422.516.
Add one row per submission per H-number with the citation, the CMS module it is filed through, the frequency and the exact due date for the coming twelve months.

Add the fixed anchors explicitly: bid and Plan Benefit Package by the first Monday in June, MLR report by the last Monday in July, Part C Reporting Requirements annual data by the last Monday in February, ANOC and EOC delivered to enrollees by 30 September.
Archive the prior inventory with a version date so the change between years is visible.
checklist.done: a versioned row inventory exists with one row per submission per H-number, each carrying a citation and a dated deadline.

checklist.step: Add the event-driven clocks that the calendar must also police
actions: Add monitoring rows for the case-level clocks: 14 calendar days for a standard organization determination on a service request, 72 hours expedited, 30 days for a standard reconsideration of a service request, 60 days for a payment reconsideration, 30 days to acknowledge and resolve a grievance, and 60 days from the adverse notice for an enrollee to request reconsideration.
For each clock, name the operational system that timestamps it and the report that measures compliance.
Set the monitoring frequency to at least monthly and name the operations owner who receives the breach list.
Link each clock row to the CFR paragraph that sets it so the calendar carries its own authority.
checklist.done: every case-level timeframe has a monitoring row with a timestamp source, a monthly report and a named operations owner.

checklist.step: Name a preparer, reviewer and submitter on every row
actions: Assign each row a preparer, an independent reviewer and an authorised HPMS submitter, and confirm the reviewer never equals the preparer.
Confirm each named HPMS submitter holds an active HPMS user account with the right module role, and request access removal for leavers the same week.
Record a named backup for every submitter so no row depends on one person.
Publish the ownership list to the Compliance Committee and refresh it each quarter.
checklist.done: no row lacks a preparer, an independent reviewer, an authorised submitter and a named backup.

checklist.step: Load the rows into the tracker and arm the reminders
actions: Create a tracker task per row with the due date, citation, owner and evidence checklist attached.
Set reminders at T-45, T-21, T-7 and T-1 to the preparer and an automatic escalation to the Compliance Officer at T-3 when the task is not in Prepared status.
Add internal cut-off dates ahead of each CMS date: data freeze, preparation complete, review complete, submission ready.
Verify the reminder fired on the first row after go-live rather than assuming the configuration works.
checklist.done: every row is a tracker task with internal cut-offs and reminders proven to fire.

checklist.step: Sweep new CMS guidance into the calendar within five business days
actions: Read every HPMS memo and Federal Register MA rule as it is issued and record it in the guidance log with the date received.
For each, decide whether it creates a new submission, moves a due date, changes a data definition or changes nothing, and write the reasoning on the log line.
Where it changes the calendar, open or amend the row within 5 business days and notify the preparer and reviewer.
Report the guidance log and its calendar impact to the Compliance Committee monthly.
checklist.done: every HPMS memo in the period has a logged disposition and any calendar change is made within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Schedule the annual utilization management committee review as a calendar row
actions: Create a row for the utilization management committee's annual review of prior authorization and internal coverage criteria required by 42 CFR 422.137(d), with the meeting date and the minutes as evidence.

Add a linked row for the public posting of prior authorization policies and for the continuity-of-coverage requirement under 422.138 that honours an approved authorization for at least 90 days after an enrollee switches plans mid-year.
Name the Medical Director chair and the committee membership requirement on the row so a quorum failure is visible.
Attach the committee charter to the row as the standing authority.
checklist.done: the annual UM committee review, the policy posting and the 90-day continuity duty each hold a dated calendar row with named evidence.

checklist.step: Freeze the source data ahead of each submission
actions: On the row's data freeze date, run the extract that feeds the submission and store it as an immutable snapshot named by row, contract and freeze date.
Run the standing validation set (record counts, date ranges, null keys, duplicate case identifiers, out-of-contract members) and record the results on the row.
Reconcile the snapshot totals to the operational system of record and explain any variance over 0.5% before the preparer starts.
Refuse to release the snapshot with an open validation failure; escalate to the Regulatory Reporting Manager instead.
checklist.done: each submission is built from a frozen, validated and reconciled snapshot stored under its calendar row.

checklist.step: Prepare the submission and hand it to the reviewer
actions: Build the file in the exact layout and value set given in the current Part C Reporting Requirements technical specifications for that section.
Run the layout validator over the file and clear every field-level error before handing it on.
Write a two-page preparation note stating the data source, the frozen snapshot identifier, the population definition and any judgement applied.
Move the tracker task to Prepared and assign it to the named reviewer at least 5 business days before the CMS date.
checklist.done: a validated file and a preparation note reach the reviewer at least 5 business days before the deadline.

checklist.step: Review and sign off before submission
actions: Re-read the technical specification for the section and check the population definition the preparer used against it, not against last period's file.
Recompute at least three totals independently from the frozen snapshot and compare to the file.
Compare the current figures to the prior period and challenge any movement over 20% in writing.
Record the sign-off with name, date and the checks performed on the tracker task.
checklist.done: a dated reviewer sign-off records recomputed totals and a written explanation of every material movement.

checklist.step: Submit through HPMS and capture the confirmation
actions: Log in to HPMS, open the module named on the calendar row, select the contract and the reporting period, and upload the reviewed file.
Wait for the module to return an accepted status rather than closing the browser at upload.
Save the confirmation page with its submission identifier and timestamp to the row's evidence pack.
Set the tracker task to Submitted with the submitted date and identifier recorded on the row.
checklist.done: the row shows an accepted HPMS status, a saved confirmation identifier and a recorded submitted date.

checklist.step: Clear rejections and resubmit inside the window
actions: Check submission status the next business day and open any rejection or validation message returned by the module.
Correct the underlying data at source, not in the output file, and re-run the freeze and validation before resubmitting.
Record both the rejected and accepted submission identifiers on the row with the reason for the rejection.
Where the correction cannot land before the CMS deadline, notify the CMS Account Manager in writing the same day and log the notification.
checklist.done: no row is left in a rejected state and every rejection carries a cause and a corrected submission identifier.

checklist.step: Report calendar health to the Compliance Committee monthly
actions: Produce a monthly dashboard of rows due, rows submitted on time, rows late, rows rejected and rows added or removed by new guidance.
List every case-level clock breach count from the monitoring rows next to its regulatory timeframe.
Escalate any row that missed a CMS deadline to the committee with the root cause and the control change made.
Minute the committee's acceptance and the actions assigned.
checklist.done: a minuted monthly report shows on-time rate, late rows, clock breaches and the control change behind each miss.

checklist.step: Log and disposition every timeliness failure
actions: Open a GRC issue for each late, missed or rejected submission naming the row, the contract, the CMS date and the actual date.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (row missing from calendar, data freeze slipped, reviewer unavailable, HPMS access lapsed, source data defect) and an owner.
Require a calendar or access control change as part of remediation, not just a repeat commitment.
Close the issue only after the next occurrence of that row is submitted on time.
checklist.done: every timeliness failure has an issue, a root cause, a control change and an on-time next occurrence before closure.

checklist.step: Prove the calendar is complete against the regulatory source twice a year
actions: Take the current Part C Reporting Requirements technical specifications section list and the HPMS module list and tick each one to a calendar row.
Walk 42 CFR 422.516 and 422.503(b)(4) paragraph by paragraph and confirm each reporting or monitoring duty appears somewhere in the inventory.
Add any missing row immediately and log its absence as a compliance-program exception.
Have the Head of Compliance sign the completeness attestation with the date and the source versions used.
checklist.done: a signed completeness attestation maps every specification section and CFR reporting duty to a calendar row.

checklist.step: Retain the timeliness evidence for ten years
actions: Move each closed row's evidence pack (frozen snapshot identifier, submitted file, preparation note, reviewer sign-off, HPMS confirmation) into the repository indexed by contract, section and period.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d) and set a legal hold flag available for program audits.
Confirm retrieval by contract plus period returns the confirmation identifier within one search.
Record the index date on the calendar row before it is archived.
checklist.done: every closed row's evidence pack is indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by contract and period.

testing.step: Build the population of calendar rows due in the quarter
actions: Export every tracker task with a CMS due date inside the quarter across all H-numbers, with owner, citation, due date and status.
Add rows closed early and rows deleted during the quarter, so a deleted obligation cannot vanish from the test.
Reconcile the export count to the calendar inventory version in force at quarter start and explain the difference.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and record count.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the quarter-start inventory and includes deleted and early-closed rows.

testing.step: Sweep the quarter's HPMS memos for obligations missing from the calendar
actions: List every HPMS memo and Federal Register MA rule issued in the quarter from the HPMS memo archive.
For each, decide independently whether it creates or moves a submission, without reading the guidance log first.
Compare your conclusion to the guidance log disposition and to the calendar, and treat any obligation absent from the calendar as a fail.
Record memo number, date, your conclusion and the calendar row reference in the workpaper.
testing.done: every quarter memo has an independent disposition and any obligation missing from the calendar is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of rows tied to a statutory anchor date (bid, MLR report, Part C Reporting Requirements annual data, ANOC and EOC delivery).
Take 20 further rows selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, minimum 30 rows in total.
Take 100% of rows that were late, rejected or deleted in the quarter.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every anchor-date row and every late, rejected or deleted row.

testing.step: Re-derive the due date for each sampled row from the regulatory source
actions: Read the cited CFR paragraph or technical specification section and compute the due date yourself before looking at the calendar value.

Check the anchor rules literally, for example the first Monday in June for the bid and the last Monday in July for the MLR report, rather than accepting a fixed calendar date carried over from last year.
Compare to the recorded due date; a right date reached from a wrong or stale citation is still an exception.
Capture the source page you relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independently derived due date with the source page captured.

testing.step: Trace each sampled row to an HPMS confirmation
actions: Open the HPMS module named on the row, select the contract and period, and read the submission status, identifier and timestamp.
Compare the identifier and timestamp to the confirmation retained in the evidence pack and treat any mismatch or missing confirmation as a fail.
Confirm the accepted submission, not a superseded rejected one, is the evidence being relied on.
Capture the HPMS status screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled row traces to an accepted HPMS submission whose identifier matches the retained evidence.

testing.step: Measure timeliness and recompute the case-level clocks
actions: Compute days early or late for every sampled row as accepted submission date minus re-derived due date.
Pull 40 organization determination and reconsideration cases from the quarter and recompute elapsed time from request receipt to notification.

Compare each to its regulatory timeframe: 14 calendar days standard service, 72 hours expedited, 30 days for a standard service reconsideration, 60 days for a payment reconsideration, 30 days for grievance resolution.
Reconcile your breach count to the monitoring report count and investigate any difference in the timestamp definition used.
testing.done: row timeliness and case-clock breach counts are independently recomputed and reconciled to the monitoring reports.

testing.step: Test segregation between preparer, reviewer and submitter
actions: For each sampled row, compare the preparer, reviewer and submitter names on the tracker task.
Treat any row where the reviewer equals the preparer, or where the sign-off is dated after the submission timestamp, as an exception.
Pull the HPMS user access list and confirm every submitter is still an employee with an active account and the correct module role.
Flag any submission made under a shared or leaver account as a control failure.
testing.done: no sampled row shows a preparer-reviewer overlap, a back-dated sign-off, or a submission under a leaver or shared account.

testing.step: Re-perform the completeness attestation
actions: Take the current Part C Reporting Requirements section list and tick each section to a calendar row without using the attestation as a guide.
Walk 42 CFR 422.516 and 422.503(b)(4)(vi) and confirm each reporting, monitoring and auditing duty maps to a row.
List every unmapped duty as a completeness failure with the citation.
Compare your mapping to the signed attestation and note any duty the attestation claimed but the calendar does not carry.
testing.done: an independent mapping of specification sections and CFR duties to rows exists, with every unmapped duty listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the row, contract, citation and what failed.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (row missing, stale citation, data freeze slipped, reviewer overlap, HPMS access lapsed, confirmation not retained) and an owner.
Set a remediation date, and for any missed CMS deadline open a self-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel the same week.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time rate and the completeness failure count against the zero-missed-deadline and zero-unmapped-duty thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with a workpaper reference behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared, reviewed or submitted no row in the quarter, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any missed deadline to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper by quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time rate and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Market Conduct Compliance owns the written procedure set for the MA quality improvement and chronic care improvement programs; the Medical Director chairs the QI committee that approves the clinical content

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.152(a) and (b) (quality improvement program and QIP), 422.152(c) (chronic care improvement program), and 422.101(a) and (b) (compliance with basic benefits and coverage rules), re-read on eCFR at each annual procedure review

In-scope processes.value: Chronic care improvement program design and operation: enrollee identification for multiple or severe chronic conditions, care management enrolment and outreach, monitoring and reassessment, plus the QI program and QIP procedures and the health risk assessment process feeding them

In-scope systems.value: Approved procedures with version and effective date held in the controlled document repository; the identification and stratification logic lives in the data warehouse and the case work in the care management case tool

Compliance procedure documented.value: CCIP and QI Program Procedure set — identification criteria and stratification thresholds, outreach script and attempt rules, care plan content, monitoring cadence, graduation and re-stratification rules, and the QI committee reporting pack definition

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Quality Improvement Committee with the Medical Director as chair and countersigned by the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager; reviewed at least annually and on any change to 422.152 or the CMS CCIP reporting guidance

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual review of every procedure by its anniversary date, aligned to the CCIP and QIP submission cycle in HPMS and to the Part C Reporting Requirements annual data due on the last Monday in February

Deadline reminders configured.value: Document repository review reminders at 90, 45 and 15 days before each procedure's annual review date, escalating to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager when a procedure passes its review date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Every version of each procedure with its approval minute, effective date, redline against the prior version and training completion record, held 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A procedure past its review date, a procedure in use without QI committee approval, or an operational practice that departs from the approved text is logged with root cause and a document or process fix

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off any procedure kept in force past its review date and every departure between practice and approved text

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every controlled procedure in the CCIP and QI procedure set across all H-numbers, plus a sample of CCIP enrollee cases worked in the period under those procedures

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a procedure in operational use without a current QI committee approval; any procedure more than 30 days past its annual review date is a fail; any sampled case worked contrary to the approved identification or monitoring rule is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual review cycle; the document currency test runs annually at the cycle close, with a semi-annual walkthrough of practice against text on the CCIP identification and monitoring steps

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not author, approve or operate any procedure in the tested set

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual CCIP and QI procedure currency workpaper (procedure inventory, approval trace, case walkthrough, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository indexed by contract year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Procedure inventory with version, approval date and QI committee minute reference, plus the CCIP description as submitted to CMS, producible for a CMS program audit or SNP care coordination review within 15 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager answers CMS audit requests for procedure documents; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement that a procedure did not exist or was not followed

checklist.step: Inventory every procedure the regulation demands
actions: Walk 42 CFR 422.152(a), (b) and (c) and 422.101(a) and (b) paragraph by paragraph and list every activity the text requires the plan to carry out.
Map each activity to an existing controlled procedure by document number, or mark it as a gap with the citation attached.
Record for each procedure its owner, approver, version, effective date and next review date on one inventory sheet.
Open a drafting task for every gap with a due date inside the current review cycle.
checklist.done: each requirement in 422.152 and 422.101 maps to a numbered procedure or an open drafting task with a due date.

checklist.step: Write the CCIP enrollee identification criteria into the procedure
actions: State the chronic conditions in scope by name and by diagnosis code family (for example diabetes, heart failure, COPD, chronic kidney disease) so identification is reproducible.

State the severity and multiplicity rule that puts an enrollee in scope, for example two or more listed conditions, or one condition with an inpatient admission or emergency visit in the last twelve months.
Name the data sources the rule runs on: encounter and claims history, pharmacy fills, health risk assessment responses and provider referral.
State how often the identification run executes and who signs the resulting cohort list.
checklist.done: the procedure states named conditions, a testable multiplicity and severity rule, the data sources and the run frequency.

checklist.step: Build and document the stratification and cohort logic
actions: Implement the identification rule as a documented query against the warehouse and record the table, field and code set used for each criterion.
Produce the cohort with member id, contract, conditions met, severity marker and stratification tier, and store the run as a dated snapshot.
Reconcile the cohort count to the prior run and explain any movement over 10% by cause (code set change, new claims runout, eligibility change).
Hand the signed cohort file and the query documentation to the care management team and attach both to the procedure record.
checklist.done: the identification logic is documented field by field, produces a dated cohort snapshot, and period-on-period movement is explained.

checklist.step: Write the outreach and enrolment rules
actions: State the outreach attempt rule: number of call attempts, spacing in days, times of day varied, and the written follow-up sent when calls fail.
State the enrolment consent wording, the opt-out handling and how a refusal is recorded so the member is not re-solicited outside the stated interval.
State the language and accessibility requirement, including interpreter access and alternate formats for enrollees who need them.
Define the case record fields that must be completed at enrolment so a later audit can see the trigger, the contact history and the consent.
checklist.done: the procedure fixes attempt counts, spacing, consent and opt-out handling, accessibility, and the mandatory case fields.

checklist.step: Write the care plan and monitoring mechanism
actions: State the care plan contents: problem list, measurable goals, interventions, the responsible clinician and the enrollee's own agreed actions.
State the monitoring cadence by stratification tier, for example monthly contact for high tier and quarterly for moderate, with the trigger events that force an unscheduled review.
State the reassessment rule that moves an enrollee between tiers or graduates them out, and who authorises it.
State the escalation route to the treating physician and the timeframe for acting on a clinical red flag.
checklist.done: the procedure specifies care plan content, tier-based contact cadence, reassessment and graduation rules, and a clinical escalation timeframe.

checklist.step: Tie the CCIP into the wider quality improvement program
actions: Write the QI program procedure so it names the CCIP, the quality improvement projects and the chronic care measures as its components, as 422.152(a) requires.
State the QI committee's membership, quorum, meeting frequency and the standing agenda items, including CCIP performance.
State the measure set used to judge CCIP effectiveness and the data source for each measure.
Attach the QI program description as submitted to CMS to the procedure record so the internal text and the external description cannot drift.
checklist.done: the QI program procedure names its components, its committee governance and its measure set, and links to the description filed with CMS.

checklist.step: Have Regulatory Counsel check the drafted text against the citations
actions: Read each drafted procedure against 42 CFR 422.152(a), (b) and (c) and 422.101(a) and (b) and mark any requirement the text softens or omits.
Strike aspirational wording that promises less than the regulation requires, for example replacing a stated timeframe with a best-efforts phrase.
Confirm the citation block at the head of each procedure quotes the current paragraph text and its date.
Return marked drafts with a written clearance note naming the paragraphs checked.
checklist.done: every procedure carries a counsel clearance note listing the paragraphs checked and no requirement is softened in the text.

checklist.step: Take the procedure set through the QI committee for approval
actions: Circulate the drafts and redlines to the QI committee at least 5 business days before the meeting.
Record attendance against the quorum requirement and confirm the Medical Director chaired.
Capture the approval resolution per document number, with the version approved and its effective date.
Publish the minute to the document repository and link it to each approved procedure record.
checklist.done: each procedure has a minuted QI committee approval naming its version number, effective date and the quorum met.

checklist.step: Publish the approved versions and retire the superseded ones
actions: Publish each approved procedure with its document number, version, effective date, owner and next review date in the metadata.
Mark the prior version superseded and remove it from the operational library so staff cannot reach it from the intranet.
Store the redline between versions with the approval minute reference.
Set the review reminder on the record for one year from the effective date.
checklist.done: only the approved version is reachable operationally, and each record carries version, effective date and an armed review reminder.

checklist.step: Train the staff who operate the procedures
actions: Build a course per changed procedure covering what changed, the new thresholds or timeframes, and the case fields that must now be completed.
Assign it to the named care management, contact centre and clinical review populations with a completion deadline of 30 days from the effective date.
Set a knowledge check with a pass mark and require a retake on failure.
Chase incompletes weekly and report residual non-completion to the operations manager after the deadline.
checklist.done: every named operator has a recorded completion and pass mark within 30 days of the procedure effective date.

checklist.step: Walk the approved text against what operations actually does
actions: Sit with a care manager and follow five live CCIP cases end to end from identification through outreach to the current care plan.
Compare each observed step to the approved text and record any departure, including workarounds staff describe as normal practice.
Where practice is better than the text, raise a document change; where practice is worse, raise a process defect.
Write the walkthrough note with case identifiers, date and the staff observed and file it against the procedure record.
checklist.done: a dated walkthrough note exists per procedure with every practice-to-text departure classified as a document or process defect.

checklist.step: Run the annual review of each procedure on its anniversary
actions: Open each procedure at its review date and re-read the cited CFR paragraphs and the current CMS guidance before deciding it is unchanged.
Bring in the period's CCIP measure results, walkthrough findings and complaint themes as inputs to the review.
Record the outcome as reaffirmed, amended or withdrawn, with the reviewer name and date, even where nothing changed.
Return amended procedures to the QI committee rather than issuing them under an administrative update.
checklist.done: every procedure has a dated annual review outcome supported by measure results and walkthrough findings.

checklist.step: Report CCIP performance and procedure health to the QI committee
actions: Report cohort size, enrolment rate, contact compliance against the tier cadence, graduation counts and each effectiveness measure to the committee each quarter.
Report the procedure inventory status: current, due within 90 days, and overdue by document number.
Present every open document or process defect with its owner and target date.
Minute the committee's decisions and carry them into the next report as tracked actions.
checklist.done: a minuted quarterly report shows CCIP measures, procedure currency status and every open defect with an owner.

checklist.step: Log procedure failures and drive the fix
actions: Open an issue for each overdue procedure, unapproved version in use, or practice-to-text departure found in a walkthrough.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (owner vacancy, review reminder not armed, committee cadence missed, training not delivered, system cannot support the rule) and an owner.
Require the fix to be a document change, a system change or a training change, not an unrecorded verbal instruction.
Close the issue only after the revised text is approved, published and trained.
checklist.done: every procedure failure has an issue, root cause, owner and a fix that is approved, published and trained before closure.

checklist.step: Retain every version for the CMS retention period
actions: Archive each superseded version with its approval minute, redline, effective and retirement dates into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 10-year retention label required by 42 CFR 422.504(d) so the version in force on any past date can be produced.
Confirm a search by document number and a date returns the version that was in force on that date.
Record the archive reference on the procedure inventory sheet.
checklist.done: the version in force on any past date is retrievable by document number and date under a 10-year retention label.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope procedures
actions: Export every controlled document tagged to the CCIP and QI program with document number, version, effective date, owner, approver and next review date.
Add documents retired during the period so a withdrawn procedure cannot escape the test.
Reconcile the export to the procedure inventory sheet and to the requirement map built from 422.152 and 422.101, listing any requirement with no document.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and record count.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the inventory sheet and to the CFR requirement map, with unmapped requirements listed.

testing.step: Reconcile each procedure to a QI committee approval
actions: Match every population row to a QI committee minute naming that document number and version.
Check the approval date precedes the effective date and that the minute records quorum and the Medical Director as chair.
Treat a version issued under an administrative update with no minute as an automatic exception.
List unmatched versions as exceptions with the dates they were operationally in force.
testing.done: every version in force traces to a quorate, pre-dated QI committee approval or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of procedures covering CCIP identification, monitoring and reassessment, since those carry the 422.152(c) requirements directly.
Take 10 further procedures at random with a recorded seed from the remaining set.
Take 30 CCIP enrollee cases worked in the period, stratified across tiers with a recorded seed.
Record the seeds, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every CCIP core procedure plus a tier-stratified case sample.

testing.step: Re-read the sampled text against the current regulation
actions: Open 42 CFR 422.152(a), (b) and (c) and 422.101(a) and (b) on eCFR and list what each paragraph requires before reading the procedure.
Read the sampled procedure and mark each requirement as covered, partially covered or absent, quoting the sentence relied on.
Treat a procedure that recites the regulation without stating an operational rule, threshold or timeframe as partially covered.
Capture the eCFR page and the procedure page into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled procedure has a requirement-by-requirement coverage assessment with quoted sentences and captured sources.

testing.step: Re-perform the CCIP identification run
actions: Rebuild the identification query from the procedure text alone, using the stated conditions, code families, severity rule and lookback window.
Run it over the same period as the production run and compare member counts and member identifiers.
Investigate every member in one result and not the other and classify the cause as a code set difference, a lookback difference or a rule the procedure does not actually state.
Attach both queries and the difference list to the workpaper.
testing.done: an independent identification run is compared member by member to production with every difference classified.

testing.step: Trace sampled cases to the outreach and monitoring rules
actions: For each sampled case, read the contact history and count outreach attempts and their spacing against the procedure rule.
Confirm a care plan exists with the required contents and that its goals are measurable rather than generic.
Recompute the contact cadence achieved against the tier requirement and record months where contact was missed.
Confirm any tier change or graduation carries the authorisation the procedure requires.
testing.done: each sampled case is measured against the attempt rule, care plan content rule and tier cadence, with misses counted.

testing.step: Test procedure currency and training completion
actions: Compute days past review date for every population row and list anything more than 30 days overdue as a fail.
For each procedure changed in the period, pull the training completion report for the named operator population.
Compare completion dates to the 30-day-from-effective-date requirement and list late or missing completions by person and role.
Check that staff who worked the sampled cases had completed the training version in force at the time.
testing.done: overdue procedures and late or missing training completions are quantified, including for the staff who worked the sampled cases.

testing.step: Compare the internal procedure to the description filed with CMS
actions: Retrieve the CCIP and QI program description as submitted to CMS through HPMS for the contract year.
Compare the target population, intervention and measure set described to CMS against the approved internal procedure.
Treat any difference in population definition or intervention as an exception, since the plan is operating a programme it did not describe.
Capture both documents into the workpaper with the differences marked.
testing.done: the CMS-filed description and the internal procedure agree on population, intervention and measures, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the document number, version and the requirement or case affected.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list (requirement not mapped, no committee approval, review overdue, logic differs from text, training not delivered, filed description drifted) and an owner.
Set a remediation date, and where enrollees were not monitored to the stated cadence require an outreach catch-up plan with a completion date.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where enrollees were affected, a catch-up plan.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the procedure currency rate, the case compliance rate and the unmapped requirement count against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with a workpaper reference behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored, approved and operated none of the tested procedures, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the QI Committee and the Compliance Committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper by contract year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, currency and case compliance rates and committee reporting dates is filed.
