checklist.step: Determine MCAS participation state by state for the data year
actions: Log in to the NAIC MCAS portal and open the data-year participation requirements page listing the participating states and lines for each MCAS blank.
For each licensed legal entity, cross the state licensure list against the participating states and record whether the entity wrote a reportable line in that state during the data year.

Apply each state's reporting threshold (commonly 50 policies or contracts in force in the line) using policy counts pulled from the policy administration extract, and record the tested count next to the in/out call.
Write the state-by-state determination onto one participation matrix with the reason for every out-of-scope call, and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager countersign it by 31 March.
checklist.done: a countersigned participation matrix shows an in/out call, a tested policy count and a reason for every entity/state/line combination.

checklist.step: Confirm the MCAS Administrator and user access before the cycle opens
actions: In the MCAS portal open the user administration page and confirm the designated MCAS Administrator of record is a current employee in the reporting team.
Add or reactivate preparer accounts for this cycle's named preparers and remove access for anyone who has left or changed role since last cycle.
Confirm the attesting officer's account can reach the attestation function by having them log in and open a prior-year submission.
Record the access review date and the user list on the filing calendar row.
checklist.done: the MCAS Administrator, preparers and attesting officer all hold working portal access and the access review is dated on the calendar row.

checklist.step: Pull the data-year Data Call & Definitions and identify what changed
actions: Download the data-year MCAS Data Call & Definitions for each blank the group files and store them in the procedure record with their version dates.
Redline the interrogatory list and definitions against the prior year and list every added, removed or redefined data element.
Walk the delta list with the Data Analyst who owns the source mapping and agree which extract queries must change.
Brief the preparers on the definition changes in a recorded session before extract build starts.
checklist.done: a dated redline of the Data Call & Definitions exists and every changed element is assigned to a named mapping change.

checklist.step: Map every interrogatory to a named source field
actions: For each MCAS interrogatory, record the source system, table and field, the population filter and any derivation logic on the mapping sheet.
Anchor claims interrogatories to the claims platform tables, grievance and appeal counts to the case management extract, and policy counts to the policy administration extract, naming each table.

Flag any interrogatory whose definition the sources cannot answer exactly, and agree the documented approximation with the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager in writing rather than leaving it implicit.
Version the mapping sheet and attach it to the procedure record.
checklist.done: every interrogatory has a field-level source mapping and every approximation is documented and agreed in writing.

checklist.step: Freeze and validate the data-year extract
actions: Run the mapped extract queries over the full data year on the agreed freeze date and store the output as an immutable snapshot named by entity, blank and freeze date.
Run the validation set — record counts by month, duplicate claim identifiers, null keys, dates outside the data year, members outside the entity — and record the results.
Reconcile extract claim counts and paid totals to the claims platform month-end reports and explain any variance over 0.5% before release.
Release the snapshot to the preparers only after every validation failure is cleared or documented, and record the snapshot identifier on the calendar row.
checklist.done: a frozen, validated snapshot reconciled to the claims platform is released with its identifier on the calendar row.

checklist.step: Build the interrogatory workbook from the frozen snapshot
actions: Compute each interrogatory from the frozen snapshot only, keeping one workbook tab per blank with the formula or query reference visible next to each figure.
Carry the prior-year submitted value in an adjacent column and compute the year-on-year movement for every interrogatory.
Write a preparation note stating the snapshot identifier, the population filters applied and every judgement or approximation used.
Hand the workbook and note to the reviewer at least 10 business days before 30 June.
checklist.done: a workbook computed solely from the frozen snapshot, with prior-year comparatives and a preparation note, reaches the reviewer 10 business days before the deadline.

checklist.step: Run the MCAS edits and ratio benchmarks before submission
actions: Run the portal's validation edits in draft mode and clear every hard edit; document the response to each soft edit warning rather than clicking through it.

Compute the MCAS scorecard ratios (for example claims paid within 30 days, grievances per 1,000 policies, denial rate) and compare each to the prior year and to the published NAIC ratio distribution where available.
Draft a written explanation for every ratio likely to sit outside the interquartile range, because those drive state analyst follow-up.
File the edit results and outlier explanations in the evidence pack.
checklist.done: all hard edits are cleared, every soft edit has a documented response, and each expected outlier ratio carries a pre-written explanation.

checklist.step: Review the workbook against statutory and operational totals
actions: Reconcile MCAS premium and policy counts to the statutory annual statement state pages for the same entity and year, and document any definitional differences (written vs in-force, line mapping).
Recompute at least five interrogatories independently from the frozen snapshot and compare to the workbook.
Challenge in writing any year-on-year movement over 20% and accept only cause-based explanations tied to volumes or process changes.
Record the review sign-off with name, date and the checks performed.
checklist.done: a dated reviewer sign-off records the statutory reconciliation, five recomputed interrogatories and an explanation for every material movement.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer attestation
actions: Present the reviewed workbook, the preparation note and the outlier explanations to the attesting officer with the reviewer sign-off attached.
Have the officer complete the MCAS attestation in the portal confirming the data is complete and accurate to the best of their knowledge.
Record the attestation date and attesting officer name on the calendar row; the attestation must pre-date or accompany the submission, never follow it.
File a copy of the attestation text in the evidence pack.
checklist.done: the portal attestation is completed by the named officer on or before the submission date and recorded on the calendar row.

checklist.step: Submit each blank through the MCAS portal by its deadline
actions: In the MCAS portal select the entity, data year and blank, key or upload the reviewed interrogatory values, and re-run the final validation.
Submit each participating state's blank no later than 30 June for the Health blank (30 April for any P&C or L&A blanks the group owes) and wait for the accepted status.
Save the confirmation page with its submission timestamp for every state into the evidence pack.
Set each calendar row to Submitted with the date and confirmation reference.
checklist.done: every participating state shows an accepted portal status with a saved confirmation dated on or before the blank's deadline.

checklist.step: Monitor post-submission status and correct rejections at source
actions: Check the portal status for every submitted blank the next business day and open any rejection or resubmission request.
Correct errors in the workbook and its source mapping, not by keying different numbers into the portal, and re-run the reviewer check on the changed interrogatories.
Record both the original and corrected submission timestamps and the cause on the calendar row.
Log every resubmission as an exception in the filing tracker.
checklist.done: no blank is left rejected, and every resubmission carries a cause, a re-review and both timestamps on its row.

checklist.step: Prepare and upload the CMS aggregate bid by the first Monday in June
actions: Complete the CMS Bid Pricing Tool workbook for every plan benefit package, covering projected revenue, medical and administrative cost, and gain/loss margin per 42 CFR 422.254(a).
Obtain the qualified actuary's certification of the bid assumptions and attach it to each BPT.
In HPMS open the Bid Submission module, upload the BPT and Plan Benefit Package files for each H-number/PBP, and resolve every upload validation before the first Monday in June.
Save the HPMS bid confirmation with its timestamp for each PBP into the evidence pack and onto the calendar row — a bid not submitted in the required form by the deadline is not approved.
checklist.done: every H-number/PBP shows an accepted HPMS bid upload with an actuarial certification, timestamped on or before the first Monday in June.

checklist.step: Certify the data that determines payment
actions: Review the summary of the bid data, enrollment figures and encounter/risk-adjustment data supporting payment with the Product / Filing Actuary and the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Execute the 42 CFR 422.504(l) certification in HPMS attesting, based on best knowledge, information and belief, to the accuracy, completeness and truthfulness of the data.
Record the certification date and certifying officer on the calendar row.
File the certification text and the supporting summary in the evidence pack.
checklist.done: the 422.504(l) certification is executed in HPMS by the accountable officer and recorded with its supporting summary.

checklist.step: Answer state ratio inquiries and bid desk questions by their stated dates
actions: Log every state MCAS analyst inquiry and CMS bid desk question with its received date and stated response date.
Answer ratio inquiries from the pre-written outlier explanations, extending them with data rather than adjectives, and route bid desk questions to the Product / Filing Actuary.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any response that concedes a data error or restatement before it is sent.
File each inquiry and response pair in the evidence pack against the state and data year.
checklist.done: every inquiry is answered by its stated date with the response filed, and any concession of error is counsel-cleared.

checklist.step: Retain the cycle evidence for ten years
actions: Move the cycle evidence pack — participation matrix, mapping sheet, frozen snapshot identifier, workbook, edit results, attestation, portal confirmations, BPT certifications and HPMS bid confirmations — into the repository indexed by entity, blank and data year.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm a search by entity and data year returns the MCAS confirmation and the bid confirmation in one query.
Record the index date on the closed calendar rows.
checklist.done: the full cycle evidence pack is indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by entity and data year.

testing.step: Build the population of filings the group owed for the year
actions: Rebuild the required-filing list independently: cross the group's state licensure register against the NAIC data-year participation states, and pull the H-number/PBP list for the contract year from HPMS.
Compare the rebuilt list to the participation matrix and the filing calendar, and list every filing owed but absent from the calendar.
Include blanks marked out of scope so the threshold calls are testable.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and record count.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt filing list reconciles to the participation matrix and calendar, with omissions listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the participation threshold call for sampled states
actions: Select ten entity/state combinations including at least three marked out of scope.
Recompute the in-force policy count for the line and data year from the policy administration extract without reading the matrix's tested count first.
Compare your count and in/out conclusion to the matrix; a right call resting on an undocumented count is still an exception.
Capture the portal participation page and your count query into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independently recomputed threshold test compared to the matrix call.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of submitted MCAS blanks and 100% of H-number/PBP bid uploads, since each carries its own deadline.
Within the blanks, select 25 interrogatories at random with a recorded seed, always including the claims-timeliness and grievance-count interrogatories.
Take 100% of resubmitted or restated items.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers every blank and bid, and always includes the claims and grievance interrogatories.

testing.step: Recompute sampled interrogatories from the frozen snapshot
actions: Open the frozen snapshot named on the calendar row and recompute each sampled interrogatory using only the Data Call & Definitions text, not the preparer's workbook formulas.
Compare your value to the submitted value and treat any difference beyond the MCAS edit tolerance as an exception.
Where your value differs because of an undocumented approximation, log a documentation exception even if the number is defensible.
Attach your recomputation file to the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled interrogatory is independently recomputed from the frozen snapshot with differences classified.

testing.step: Trace every submission to a portal confirmation
actions: In the MCAS portal open each sampled blank's submission history and read the status and timestamp; in HPMS open the Bid Submission module for each PBP and read the accepted status.
Compare portal timestamps to the confirmations retained in the evidence pack and treat any mismatch or missing confirmation as a fail.
Confirm the accepted submission, not a superseded rejected one, is the evidence relied on.
Capture the portal history screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: every blank and bid traces to an accepted portal record whose timestamp matches the retained confirmation.

testing.step: Recompute the deadlines and measure timeliness
actions: Recompute the due date per filing from the source: 30 June for the Health MCAS blank, 30 April for P&C and L&A blanks, and the first Monday in June of the calendar year for the bid — computing the actual first-Monday date rather than copying last year's.
Compare the accepted timestamp to the recomputed due date and record days early or late for every filing.
Measure resubmitted items against the accepted resubmission, and treat any acceptance after the due date as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
Record the deadline maths on one timeliness schedule in the workpaper.
testing.done: every filing shows a recomputed deadline and measured filing date with no unreported late acceptance.

testing.step: Verify the attestation and certification chain
actions: Confirm each blank's portal attestation names an authorised officer and is dated on or before the submission timestamp.
Confirm each bid carries a qualified actuary's certification and that the 42 CFR 422.504(l) certification was executed in HPMS by the accountable officer.
Confirm the reviewer sign-off pre-dates the attestation, so nothing was attested unreviewed.
Treat a missing, post-dated or wrongly-signed attestation as an exception regardless of data accuracy.
testing.done: every filing shows review, attestation and certification in the right order by the right people.

testing.step: Reconcile submitted figures to the operational systems of record
actions: Tie total claims received and paid counts in the submitted blank to the claims platform month-end reports for the data year.
Tie grievance and appeal counts to the case management system's closed-case totals for the same period.
Tie MCAS premium to the statutory state page and document the definitional bridge for any expected difference.
Treat an unexplained variance over 0.5% on any tie as an exception.
testing.done: claims, grievance and premium figures tie to their systems of record within tolerance or carry a documented bridge.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception naming the entity, blank or PBP, the interrogatory or deadline affected and the regulatory impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (participation call undocumented, mapping wrong, snapshot bypassed, review skipped, portal access lapsed, deadline miscomputed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; for any late filing or restated submission open a notification assessment with Regulatory Counsel for the affected state or CMS.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time rate and the interrogatory accuracy rate against the zero-late-filing threshold and the edit tolerance.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with a workpaper reference behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared, reviewed, attested and submitted nothing in the cycle, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper by data year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time and accuracy rates and a committee reporting date is filed.

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly measurement of every conduct metric across all H-numbers: organization determination and reconsideration clock compliance, grievance resolution timeliness, CTM complaint rates and SLA compliance, IRE auto-forward timeliness and overturn rate, call-center accessibility, marketing and rapid-disenrollment indicators, and the CCIP effectiveness measures required by 422.152(c)

In-scope systems.value: Metric marts fed from the appeals/grievance case tool, claims platform, contact-center telephony and the HPMS CTM extract; the quarterly pack is published from the BI platform with each metric linked to its frozen extract

Compliance procedure documented.value: Conduct Metric Monitoring Procedure — a metric dictionary giving each metric a numerator, denominator, source extract, regulatory benchmark with citation, tolerance band and escalation rule, plus the quarterly production timetable

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Compliance Officer and reviewed each October when CMS publishes the annual Star Ratings Technical Notes, and re-opened whenever a CFR timeframe or CTM SLA changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly pack issued within 20 business days of quarter end; monthly case-clock breach lists to operations within 10 business days of month end; CTM cases worked to the CMS resolution SLAs (2 calendar days immediate-need, 7 days urgent, 30 days standard)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tracker reminders at quarter end +5, +10 and +15 business days to the metric preparers, escalating to the Head of Compliance at +18 if the pack is not in Review status

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each quarterly pack, its frozen metric extracts, the benchmark source references, committee minutes and breach remediation records retained 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any metric breaching its regulatory benchmark, any metric red for two consecutive quarters, and any metric omitted from the pack is logged with root cause, an owner and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off the closure of every benchmark breach and any change to a metric definition or tolerance band

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every metric in the quarter's pack across all H-numbers, the frozen extracts behind them, the quarter's CTM download, and the case-level records underlying the clock metrics

Pass/fail thresholds.value: The pack must contain 100% of dictionary metrics; a recomputed metric differing from the reported value by more than 1% is a fail; any breaching metric not escalated per the procedure is a fail regardless of size

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; the verification test runs each quarter within 30 days of pack issuance, with the case-clock recomputation rotating across H-numbers

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not compute, review or publish any metric in the tested pack

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly conduct-metric verification workpaper (pack completeness check, extract reconciliation, metric recomputation, clock re-performance, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository by quarter

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The metric pack, the metric dictionary with citations, and breach remediation records producible for a CMS program audit compliance-program-effectiveness request or an Account Manager inquiry within 15 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager answers CMS metric and CTM inquiries; the Compliance Officer owns program-audit CPE responses; Regulatory Counsel clears any response conceding a systemic timeliness failure

checklist.step: Maintain the metric dictionary as the single definition source
actions: Keep one dictionary row per metric with numerator, denominator, source extract, benchmark, citation, tolerance band, owner and escalation rule.
Review the dictionary each October against the new Star Ratings Technical Notes and each CFR change, versioning every edit.
Reject any metric that appears in a pack without a dictionary row, and any dictionary row with no named data source.
Publish the current version to the metric preparers and the QI committee.
checklist.done: every pack metric traces to a current dictionary row with a benchmark, citation and named source.

checklist.step: Anchor every benchmark to its regulatory source
actions: Record against each clock metric its CFR timeframe: 14 calendar days standard and 72 hours expedited for organization determinations (422.568/422.572), 30 days for a standard service reconsideration and 60 days for a payment reconsideration (422.590), and 30 days for grievance resolution (422.564).

Record the CTM SLAs (2 calendar days immediate-need, 7 days urgent, 30 days standard) and the call-center standards from the current CMS call-center monitoring guidance (average hold within 2 minutes, interpreter connection within 8 minutes, disconnect rate under 5%).
Record the Star Ratings cut points for each monitored measure from the current Technical Notes, with the document version.
Capture each source page into the dictionary record so a benchmark can never be asserted from memory.
checklist.done: each benchmark carries its CFR cite, CMS guidance version or Technical Notes cut point with a captured source page.

checklist.step: Build the quarterly extract set
actions: Run the standing extract queries for the quarter: organization determinations and reconsiderations with received and decided timestamps, grievances with acknowledgement and resolution dates, IRE auto-forward records, enrollment/disenrollment transactions and CCIP cohort contact records.
Pull the contact-center interval data (hold time, interpreter connect time, disconnect rate) from the telephony platform for the quarter.
Store each extract as a dated snapshot named by metric family and quarter.
Record row counts per extract on the production log for the reconciliation step.
checklist.done: every metric family has a dated quarterly snapshot with logged row counts.

checklist.step: Validate and freeze the extracts before computation
actions: Run the validation set over each snapshot: null timestamps, decided-before-received records, duplicate case identifiers, cases outside the quarter and members outside the contract.
Reconcile case counts to the case tool's closed-case report and CTM counts to the HPMS download for the same period, explaining any difference before release.
Freeze the snapshots and refuse recomputation from live tables after the freeze.
Record validation results and the freeze date on the production log.
checklist.done: all snapshots are validated, reconciled to their systems of record and frozen with a logged freeze date.

checklist.step: Compute the determination, appeal and grievance clock metrics
actions: Compute elapsed time per case from request receipt to notification using the frozen snapshot, honouring the dictionary's timestamp definitions and any allowable extension rules.

Compute the compliance rate per clock: within 14 calendar days standard service, within 72 hours expedited, within 30 days standard service reconsideration, within 60 days payment reconsideration, within 30 days grievance resolution.
Compute the IRE auto-forward metric — cases affirmed on reconsideration forwarded to the Independent Review Entity — and its timeliness against the dictionary rule.
Publish each metric with numerator, denominator and the snapshot identifier it came from.
checklist.done: every clock metric is published with numerator, denominator, snapshot identifier and its compliance rate against the CFR timeframe.

checklist.step: Pull the CTM complaints and compute complaint metrics
actions: In HPMS open the Complaints Tracking Module and download the quarter's complaints for every H-number with category, received date and resolution date.
Compute the complaint rate per 1,000 enrollees by contract using the CMS enrollment report for the same months as the denominator.
Compute resolution SLA compliance against the 2-day immediate-need, 7-day urgent and 30-day standard timeframes.
Reconcile the CTM download count to the internal complaints log and investigate complaints present in one and not the other.
checklist.done: CTM complaint rates and SLA compliance are computed per contract and the CTM download reconciles to the internal log.

checklist.step: Compute the call-center accessibility metrics
actions: Pull the quarter's interval data for the member and prospective-member lines: average hold time, interpreter connect time and disconnect rate.
Compare each to the CMS standards (hold within 2 minutes, interpreter within 8 minutes, disconnect under 5%) and to any CMS secret-shopper or timeliness study results received in the quarter.
Compute TTY answer performance and after-hours coverage against the dictionary rule.
Hand the computed metrics with the interval extract to the metric pack owner.
checklist.done: hold, interpreter, disconnect and TTY metrics are computed from telephony interval data and compared to the CMS standards.

checklist.step: Compute the CCIP effectiveness measures
actions: From the CCIP cohort snapshot, compute enrolment rate, contact-cadence compliance by stratification tier, care-plan currency and graduation counts for the quarter.
Compute the clinical effectiveness measures named in the CCIP description filed with CMS (for example admission and readmission rates for the cohort) from the claims snapshot.
Compare each measure to its target in the CCIP description and flag misses for the QI committee, as 422.152(c) requires the program to monitor and manage the identified enrollees.
Attach the measure file to both the metric pack and the QI committee agenda.
checklist.done: CCIP enrolment, cadence and clinical measures are computed against the filed CCIP targets and routed to the QI committee.

checklist.step: Compute the marketing and enrollment conduct indicators
actions: Compute the rapid-disenrollment rate (disenrollment within 3 months of enrollment) by contract and by selling agent channel from the enrollment snapshot.
Compute agent-related complaint counts from the CTM download and the internal sales-allegation log, by agency.
Flag any agency or channel whose rapid-disenrollment or complaint rate sits above the dictionary threshold for referral to the Producer Compliance Manager.
Attach the indicator file to the metric pack.
checklist.done: rapid-disenrollment and agent-complaint indicators are computed by contract and channel with threshold breaches referred.

checklist.step: Rate every metric against its benchmark and tolerance
actions: Set each metric red, amber or green strictly by the dictionary tolerance band, not by judgement on the day.
Recompute at least three metrics independently from the frozen snapshots as a production check before rating.
Compare every metric to the prior four quarters and mark any two-consecutive-quarter red as a standing breach.
Record the rating sheet with name and date in the pack.
checklist.done: every metric carries a band-based rating, a four-quarter trend and a dated rating sheet.

checklist.step: Write breach commentary and open remediations
actions: For every red metric, write commentary stating the size of the miss, the affected contracts, the enrollee impact and the operational cause.
Open a GRC issue per breach with an owner, a remediation date and the metric level that constitutes closure.
For clock breaches, require the operations owner to produce the case-level breach list and confirm each affected case was completed, not just counted.
Link each issue to the metric's dictionary row so repeat breaches accumulate on one record.
checklist.done: every red metric has commentary, a GRC issue with an owner and closure level, and clock breaches carry a worked case list.

checklist.step: Publish the pack to the governance committees
actions: Issue the pack to the Compliance Committee within 20 business days of quarter end, with the CCIP section copied to the QI committee.
Present the standing breaches and the remediation ageing first, not buried behind green metrics.
Minute the committee's challenge and the actions assigned, and carry them into the next pack as tracked items.
File the pack and minutes in the evidence pack for the quarter.
checklist.done: the pack is issued inside 20 business days and the minutes record challenge and assigned actions.

checklist.step: Feed breaches into the monitoring and audit workplan
actions: Review every standing breach for inclusion in the compliance monitoring workplan as a focused audit, as the 422.503(b)(4)(vi) monitoring element requires.
Commission a case-level audit for any clock metric red two consecutive quarters.
Assess whether any breach meets the bar for self-identification to the CMS Account Manager and record the decision with Regulatory Counsel's advice.
Record the workplan changes in the monitoring schedule.
checklist.done: standing breaches are reflected in the monitoring workplan and each disclosure decision is recorded with counsel advice.

checklist.step: Track remediations to closure with a retest
actions: Hold each breach issue open until the metric returns inside its tolerance band for a full quarter.
Require evidence of the operational fix (roster change, system rule, script change) on the issue before closure, not just the improved number.
Have the Head of Compliance sign the closure of every benchmark breach.
Report remediation ageing in each quarterly pack until closure.
checklist.done: no breach closes without an evidenced fix, a full in-tolerance quarter and Head of Compliance sign-off.

checklist.step: Retain the pack and its extracts for ten years
actions: Move the quarter's pack, rating sheet, frozen snapshots, CTM download, minutes and breach records into the repository indexed by quarter and contract.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm a search by quarter returns the pack and every snapshot behind it.
Record the index date on the production log.
checklist.done: the pack and every underlying snapshot are indexed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by quarter.

testing.step: Verify the pack contains every dictionary metric
actions: Take the current metric dictionary version in force at quarter start and tick every row to a metric in the issued pack.
List any metric missing from the pack, added without a dictionary row, or computed under a definition differing from the dictionary.
Confirm the pack was issued within 20 business days of quarter end from the issue timestamp.
Record the completeness result as the population baseline for the test.
testing.done: every dictionary metric is accounted for in the pack, and the issue date is measured against the 20-business-day rule.

testing.step: Reconcile the frozen extracts to their systems of record
actions: Compare each snapshot's row count to the source system report for the same period: case tool closed cases, CTM download, telephony interval records, enrollment transactions.
Investigate any count difference above 0.5% and classify it as timing, filter or omission.
Confirm the metrics were computed from the frozen snapshots and not re-run against live tables after the freeze.
Record the reconciliation on one schedule in the workpaper.
testing.done: every snapshot reconciles to its system of record within tolerance and metrics trace to frozen data.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of red metrics and 100% of metrics within 2 percentage points of their benchmark.
Take 10 further metrics selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining pack.
Take 40 cases from the clock-metric populations, stratified across determination, reconsideration and grievance types with a recorded seed.
Record the seeds, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every red and near-breach metric plus a stratified case sample.

testing.step: Recompute the sampled metrics from the frozen snapshots
actions: Recompute each sampled metric using only the dictionary definition and the frozen snapshot, without reading the preparer's computation.
Compare to the reported value and treat any difference over 1% as an exception.
Where the difference stems from an undictionaried judgement call, log a definition exception even if the reported value is defensible.
Attach the recomputation files to the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled metric is independently recomputed with differences over 1% logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Re-derive each sampled benchmark from the regulator source
actions: Open the cited CFR paragraph on eCFR, or the current Technical Notes or CMS guidance document, and read the timeframe or cut point yourself before checking the dictionary value.
Confirm the dictionary benchmark matches the current source, not last year's — a stale cut point is an exception even if the metric passed.
Capture each source page into the workpaper.
List every benchmark whose source version postdates the dictionary review.
testing.done: each sampled benchmark is independently re-derived from the current regulatory source with the page captured.

testing.step: Re-perform the clock computation on the sampled cases
actions: Open each sampled case in the case tool and read the raw request-received and notification timestamps from the case history, not the reporting fields.
Recompute elapsed time against the applicable timeframe: 14 calendar days standard, 72 hours expedited, 30 days service reconsideration, 60 days payment reconsideration, 30 days grievance.
Verify any extension applied was permissible and documented in the case before excluding it from the breach count.
Compare your case-level result to the metric's classification of that case and log any difference.
testing.done: every sampled case is re-timed from raw timestamps with extensions verified and classification differences logged.

testing.step: Verify the CTM reconciliation and complaint handling
actions: Re-download the quarter's CTM complaints from HPMS for two contracts and compare counts to the pack's denominator data.
Trace five sampled complaints from CTM to the internal complaints log and to a resolution letter or call record within the SLA.
Confirm complaints resolved past SLA appear in the breach count rather than being reclassified.
Capture the CTM screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: CTM counts re-pulled from HPMS match the pack and sampled complaints trace to in-SLA resolutions or counted breaches.

testing.step: Verify breaches were escalated and remediated per the procedure
actions: For every red metric in the quarter, confirm a GRC issue exists with an owner, remediation date and closure level.
Confirm two-consecutive-quarter reds triggered the case-level audit the procedure requires.
Confirm closed breach issues carry evidence of an operational fix and a full in-tolerance quarter, plus Head of Compliance sign-off.
Treat any breach absent from GRC as an escalation failure regardless of its size.
testing.done: every breach traces to an owned GRC issue and every closure carries a fix, an in-tolerance quarter and sign-off.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per test exception naming the metric or case, the quarter and what failed.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (definition drift, stale benchmark, snapshot bypassed, timestamp misuse, escalation missed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; where a recomputation shows a regulatory clock was breached but reported compliant, open a disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the recomputation accuracy rate and the escalation compliance rate against the 1% and zero-missed-escalation thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with a workpaper reference behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who computed and published nothing in the pack, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper by quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, accuracy and escalation rates and a committee reporting date is filed.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off the closure of every mock-audit condition and every failed dry-run remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every section of the readiness index, every universe query in the catalogue, the quarter's dry-run outputs, the disclosed-issues log entries and a sample of underlying case files

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every universe must generate inside the drill window and pass layout validation with a rejected-record rate under 1%; any readiness section more than one refresh cycle stale is a fail; any known issue absent from the disclosed-issues log is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the verification test runs semi-annually, alternating a timed universe drill with a documentation-depth review, plus a full test after every CMS protocol reissue

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own any universe query, readiness section or disclosed-issue entry under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual audit-readiness verification workpaper (index completeness, timed drill results, layout validation, case-file depth review, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The readiness index itself, the latest dry-run timings and the disclosed-issues log, producible on the day a CMS engagement letter arrives; universes producible to CMS record layouts within the 15-business-day window

Regulator response path.value: The Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager is the named audit single point of contact; the Compliance Officer owns CPE responses; Regulatory Counsel reviews the pre-audit issue summary before it is sent to CMS

checklist.step: Structure the readiness file to mirror the CMS protocol areas
actions: Download the current CMS Program Audit Protocols and Data Requests from the CMS program audit page and list every protocol area applicable to the Part C contracts (ODAG, CPE, and SNPCC where SNPs are offered).
Create one controlled folder per protocol area plus standing sections for contracts and licensure, delegation agreements, policies, and the disclosed-issues summary.
Assign a named owner and a quarterly refresh date to every section in the readiness index.
Version the index and store the protocol documents beside it so the structure is traceable to the CMS source.
checklist.done: a versioned readiness index mirrors the current CMS protocol areas with a named owner and refresh date per section.

checklist.step: Build and own the universe query catalogue
actions: Build one documented query per CMS universe record layout — standard and expedited organization determinations, reconsiderations, grievances, and dismissals — producing every column in the CMS layout with the required formats (dates as CCYYMMDD, times where specified, disposition codes from the layout's value list).
Store each query in the catalogue with its layout version, source tables, owner and last-validated date.
Update the catalogue within 20 business days whenever CMS reissues a record layout, and version the change.
Prove each new or changed query against the layout with a sample output before it enters the catalogue.
checklist.done: every CMS universe layout has a catalogued, owned query whose output matches the layout column by column.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly timed universe dry-run
actions: Simulate an engagement letter by fixing a review period and running every catalogued universe query for it, timing the end-to-end production.
Validate each output against the CMS layout: column order, formats, code values, no nulls in required fields, and record counts reconciled to the case tool for the period.
Record production time per universe against the internal target (all universes complete within 10 business days, leaving buffer inside the 15-business-day engagement window).
Log any failed validation or missed timing as a GRC finding with the query owner.
checklist.done: a timed quarterly dry-run shows every universe producible inside the internal window and passing layout validation.

checklist.step: Keep the compliance-program evidence pack current
actions: Maintain in the CPE section the current standards of conduct, compliance policies, the compliance officer and committee charters, board reporting on the compliance program, the annual risk assessment, the monitoring and audit workplan with results, and disciplinary evidence — the elements of 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi).
Refresh training completion extracts quarterly from the learning system, covering employees, board members and applicable FDR staff.
File each compliance committee agenda, pack and minute within 10 business days of the meeting.
Mark each document with its period of validity so a stale version is visible on sight.
checklist.done: the CPE section holds current, dated evidence for every 422.503(b)(4)(vi) element with training extracts no older than a quarter.

checklist.step: Maintain the disclosed-issues log audit-ready
actions: Record every self-identified compliance issue in the log with the protocol area it maps to, the discovery date, root cause, remediation status and enrollee impact.
Keep the log in the format of the CMS pre-audit issue summary so it can be produced without rework when an engagement letter arrives.
Review the log monthly against new monitoring results, breach reports and metric-pack findings so nothing known is missing.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the log wording quarterly, since it will be handed to CMS verbatim.
checklist.done: the disclosed-issues log is complete against monitoring results, formatted as a pre-audit issue summary and counsel-reviewed.

checklist.step: Keep contracts, licensure and delegation documents current
actions: File the executed CMS contract and current addenda for every H-number, plus each state license and certificate of authority for the legal entities.
File every delegation agreement with first-tier entities, including the required compliance and audit provisions, with its current signature page.
Diarise expiry and renewal dates and chase re-execution 90 days ahead.
Index the section by H-number and counterparty so a CMS request can be answered same-day.
checklist.done: current executed contracts, licenses and delegation agreements are indexed by H-number with renewals diarised 90 days out.

checklist.step: Maintain FDR oversight evidence
actions: Keep the FDR inventory current: every first-tier, downstream and related entity performing Part C functions, the function delegated and the oversight owner.

File each FDR's annual oversight evidence — audit or monitoring results, corrective actions, exclusion-list screening (OIG LEIE and GSA/SAM) at hire and monthly thereafter, and compliance attestations.
Escalate any FDR with overdue oversight to the Compliance Committee.
Map each FDR file to the protocol area its function falls under so audit requests route instantly.
checklist.done: every FDR has a current oversight file with monthly exclusion screening and an oversight owner, mapped to a protocol area.

checklist.step: Run continuous case-documentation quality checks
actions: Each month sample 20 organization determination, reconsideration and grievance cases across contracts.

Check each case would survive an auditor webinar walkthrough: request receipt evidenced, clinical rationale documented, notification letter on file with the correct appeal-rights language, timestamps consistent with the universe fields.
Score the sample and feed defects to the operations owner with a correction date.
Trend the scores quarterly in the readiness report.
checklist.done: a monthly 20-case documentation sample is scored, defects are owned with dates and the trend is reported quarterly.

checklist.step: Run the annual mock program audit
actions: Issue an internal engagement letter unannounced to the audit response team, fixing the review period and the universe due date to mirror the CMS 15-business-day window.
Have the team produce the universes, then select samples and run webinar-style case walkthroughs against the CMS protocol compliance standards.
Write conditions in CMS format (condition, criteria, cause, effect) and classify severity as CMS would (immediate corrective action required versus corrective action required).
Issue the mock-audit report to the Head of Compliance and the Compliance Committee with owners and dates per condition.
checklist.done: an unannounced mock audit produced timed universes, sampled walkthroughs and a conditions report in CMS format.

checklist.step: Train and rehearse the audit response team
actions: Maintain a named audit response roster: single point of contact, universe owners per protocol area, case presenters, IT support for the webinar platform, and a scribe.
Deliver annual training on the engagement-letter timeline, universe integrity rules (no post-hoc data edits), and how to present a case file on screen without narrating beyond the record.
Rehearse the first-48-hours protocol: acknowledge the letter, stand up the war room, freeze relevant data, notify Regulatory Counsel and the executive sponsor.
Record completion for every roster member and chase gaps within 30 days.
checklist.done: a current roster exists and every member holds in-date training including the first-48-hours rehearsal.

checklist.step: Keep marketing and enrollment material evidence indexed
actions: Maintain the index of marketing materials by HPMS material ID with submission date, File-and-Use certification or approval status, and distribution dates.
File the ANOC/EOC mailing evidence for each contract year showing delivery by 30 September.
File agent training and testing records and TPMO oversight evidence for the sales channel.
Map the section to the audit request formats so material can be produced by ID on demand.
checklist.done: marketing materials, ANOC/EOC mailing evidence and agent oversight records are indexed and producible by material ID.

checklist.step: Refresh and sign the readiness index quarterly
actions: Walk every index section at quarter end: confirm the owner, check the newest document date against the refresh rule, and mark the section current or stale.
Chase every stale section to currency within 15 business days.
Sign the index refresh with date and findings.
Report index status, dry-run timings and case-quality trends to the Compliance Committee quarterly.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly index refresh shows every section current or under a 15-day cure with committee reporting.

checklist.step: Remediate readiness findings through the GRC platform
actions: Open an issue for every failed dry-run, stale section, mock-audit condition and case-quality defect trend.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (query broken by system change, owner vacancy, layout reissued unnoticed, documentation practice drift) and an owner.
Require re-execution of the failed drill or a re-sampled quality check as closure evidence.
Track ageing and escalate anything over 60 days to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every readiness finding is an owned issue closed only on a passed re-drill or re-sample, with 60-day escalation.

checklist.step: Stand ready to execute the engagement-letter protocol
actions: Keep the engagement-letter response protocol one page long and current: who acknowledges CMS, who freezes data, who produces which universe, who reviews the pre-audit issue summary and who briefs the executives.
Verify each named person and deputy quarterly against the HR roster.
Pre-draft the acknowledgement and the internal notification templates.
Test the protocol as part of the annual mock audit and update it with the lessons.
checklist.done: a current one-page protocol with verified names and pre-drafted templates exists and was exercised in the last mock audit.

checklist.step: Retain readiness evidence for ten years
actions: Archive each quarter's signed index, dry-run outputs and timings, mock-audit report and case-quality scores into the repository by quarter.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d) and keep the records available to CMS and its designees per 422.504(e).
Confirm retrieval by quarter and protocol area returns the dry-run evidence in one search.
Record the archive reference on the readiness index.
checklist.done: readiness evidence is archived by quarter under a 10-year retention label and retrievable by protocol area.

testing.step: Build the population of readiness assets
actions: Export the readiness index with every section, owner, refresh date and newest-document date, plus the universe query catalogue with layout versions.
Reconcile the index structure to the current CMS Program Audit Protocols and Data Requests, listing any protocol area or universe layout with no corresponding section or query.
Add the disclosed-issues log entries and the quarter's dry-run outputs to the population.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the current CMS protocols with every uncovered protocol area or layout listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the universe catalogue to the current CMS record layouts
actions: Download the current CMS record layouts independently and compare each catalogued query's layout version to the CMS version.
List every query built to a superseded layout as a fail regardless of dry-run results.
Confirm layout changes issued in the period reached the catalogue within the 20-business-day rule.
Record the version comparison in the workpaper.
testing.done: every catalogued query is tied to the current CMS layout version or listed as a fail.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of universe queries for the timed drill.
Take five readiness sections at random with a recorded seed, always including CPE and the disclosed-issues log.
Take 25 cases from the produced universes, stratified across determination, reconsideration and grievance types with a recorded seed.
Record the seeds, population sizes and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers every universe query and always includes CPE and the disclosed-issues log.

testing.step: Run an independent timed universe drill
actions: Fix a review period unknown to the universe owners in advance and request production of every universe, timing from request to delivery.
Measure elapsed time against the internal 10-business-day target inside the CMS 15-business-day engagement window.
Validate the outputs against the CMS layouts independently: column formats, code values, required fields, and record counts reconciled to the case tool.
Treat any universe missing the window or exceeding a 1% rejected-record rate as a fail.
testing.done: an independently timed drill shows every universe delivered in-window and passing layout validation, or failed and logged.

testing.step: Walk sampled cases as an auditor would
actions: For each sampled case, open the case file and check it against the CMS protocol compliance standard for its type: receipt evidence, clinical decision rationale, correct notification letter with appeal rights, and effectuation where required.
Compare the case-file timestamps to the universe fields for the same case and treat any inconsistency as a universe-integrity exception.
Time how long each case takes to assemble on screen and flag anything over the internal presentation target.
Record findings per case in CMS condition language.
testing.done: every sampled case is walked against the protocol standard with universe-field consistency checked and findings in condition format.

testing.step: Verify the disclosed-issues log is complete
actions: Cross the period's monitoring results, metric-pack breaches, mock-audit conditions and remediation log entries against the disclosed-issues log.
List any known issue absent from the log as a fail — an undisclosed known issue is the highest-severity readiness defect.
Confirm each log entry carries a protocol area, discovery date, root cause and remediation status.
Confirm the latest counsel review of the log wording is within the quarter.
testing.done: every known issue from monitoring and testing appears in the log with complete fields and a current counsel review.

testing.step: Verify readiness-section currency and owner assignments
actions: For each sampled section, compare the newest document date to the section's refresh rule and compute days stale.
Verify the named owner is a current employee in the stated role against the HR roster.
Open three documents per section and confirm they are final, signed versions rather than drafts.
List any section more than one refresh cycle stale as a fail.
testing.done: sampled sections show in-cycle documents, current owners and signed versions, with staleness quantified.

testing.step: Verify mock-audit conditions were remediated
actions: Trace every condition from the last mock-audit report to a GRC issue with an owner and remediation date.
For closed conditions, verify the closure evidence is a passed re-drill or re-sample, not a narrative assertion.
Confirm Head of Compliance sign-off on each closure.
Recompute ageing on open conditions and flag anything past 60 days without escalation.
testing.done: every mock-audit condition traces to an owned issue with evidence-based closure or an in-policy escalation.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the universe, section or case and what failed.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (layout drift, query defect, owner vacancy, documentation practice drift, undisclosed known issue) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; treat an undisclosed known issue as reportable to the Head of Compliance the same day.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the drill pass rate, the layout validation rate and the section currency rate against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion (audit-ready, audit-ready with exceptions, or not audit-ready) with a workpaper reference behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns no universe, section or log entry, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper by half-year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states an audit-readiness conclusion with drill, validation and currency rates and a committee date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Compliance Officer owns the remediation log for every CMS program audit condition, notice of non-compliance, warning letter and state exam finding against the MA contracts; operational owners execute the corrective actions

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(G) (prompt response to detected offenses and corrective action initiatives), 422.504(e) (CMS audit and inspection rights), and 422.752/422.756 (intermediate sanctions and civil money penalties for failures), re-read on eCFR when each finding is logged, plus the CMS program audit process timeline in the current audit protocol documents

In-scope processes.value: Intake and classification of every external finding (CMS program audit ICARs and CARs, notices of non-compliance, warning letters, one-third financial audit findings, state market conduct findings), beneficiary impact analysis and remediation, corrective action plan drafting, submission and implementation, CMS validation audit response, and closure

In-scope systems.value: The remediation log is the GRC issue register; CAP documents move through the HPMS audit module; beneficiary remediation is executed in the claims and case systems and evidenced back to the GRC issue

Compliance procedure documented.value: Exam Finding Remediation Procedure — intake and classification rules, the ICAR three-business-day clock, the 10-business-day draft report comment window, the 30-calendar-day CAP submission clock, beneficiary impact analysis standards, evidence rules per milestone, and validation audit preparation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and noted by the Compliance Committee; reviewed after every completed audit cycle and whenever CMS revises the program audit process timeline

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven clocks per finding: immediate corrective action required conditions addressed within 3 business days; comments on the CMS draft report within 10 business days; the corrective action plan submitted within 30 calendar days of the final report; validation audit readiness roughly 150 days after CAP acceptance; state exam CAPs by the date set in the exam report adoption order

Deadline reminders configured.value: Every logged finding gets clock-based reminders at 50% and 80% of its window plus a day-before alert to the action owner, escalating to the Compliance Officer and the executive sponsor when a milestone is 5 days from breach

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The finding text, classification, impact analysis, submitted CAP and CMS acceptance, milestone evidence, validation audit results and closure sign-offs retained 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A milestone missed against the CMS or state clock, a CAP rejected by CMS, a remediation that fails validation, or a repeat finding on a previously closed condition is logged as an exception with root cause and re-plan

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every CAP before submission and the closure of every finding; enrollee-impacting closures also carry the Chief Operating Officer's sign-off

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every finding logged in the period from any external source, every open finding carried in from prior periods, and the beneficiary remediation files attached to enrollee-impacting findings

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a missed ICAR, comment-window or CAP-submission clock; a milestone closed without attached evidence is a fail; a beneficiary remediation whose affected-enrollee count cannot be re-derived is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs quarterly over all findings open or closed in the quarter, with a full-cycle review after each CMS validation audit

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have owned any corrective action or drafted any tested CAP

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly remediation-timeliness workpaper (finding population, clock recomputation, milestone evidence trace, beneficiary remediation re-derivation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The remediation log export with per-finding clocks, submitted CAPs, CMS acceptances and validation results, producible for a CMS follow-up request or enforcement conference within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Compliance Officer signs CAP submissions through the HPMS audit module; Regulatory Counsel manages any enforcement correspondence under 422.752/422.756 and clears every submission that concedes non-compliance

checklist.step: Log every finding on the day it arrives
actions: Open a GRC issue the same business day for each condition in a CMS draft or final audit report, each notice of non-compliance or warning letter, each one-third financial audit finding and each state exam finding.
Copy the condition text verbatim with its citation, protocol area, classification (immediate corrective action required, corrective action required, or observation) and the source document reference.
Attach the source letter or report to the issue and link related conditions.
Notify the Compliance Officer and the affected operational executive the same day.
checklist.done: every external finding is a same-day GRC issue carrying the verbatim condition, classification and source document.

checklist.step: Start the regulatory clock on each finding
actions: Set the deadline field from the classification: corrective action within 3 business days for an ICAR, comments on a draft report within 10 business days, the CAP within 30 calendar days of the final report, and the date stated in the order for a state exam CAP.
Compute each date from the CMS letter date, counting business or calendar days exactly as the letter states, and record the computation on the issue.
Arm the 50%, 80% and day-before reminders to the action owner with escalation to the executive sponsor at 5 days from breach.
Diarise the expected validation audit window roughly 150 days after CAP acceptance.
checklist.done: every finding carries a computed regulatory deadline with armed reminders and a diarised validation window.

checklist.step: Contain ICAR conditions within three business days
actions: For each immediate corrective action required condition, stop the ongoing harm first: effectuate wrongly denied services or payments, restore wrongly terminated coverage, or halt the non-compliant process the same week.
Document the containment action, its date and the evidence (transaction identifiers, case numbers) on the GRC issue within the 3-business-day window.
Confirm to CMS through the auditor's stated channel that the immediate action is complete, in the words Regulatory Counsel clears.
Hand the underlying fix into the CAP workstream — containment never closes the finding.
checklist.done: every ICAR shows a documented containment action inside 3 business days and a cleared confirmation to CMS.

checklist.step: Quantify the beneficiary impact
actions: Write a documented query identifying every enrollee affected by the condition — denied or delayed services, misprocessed claims, wrong letters, missed appeals — over the full period the defect operated, not just the audit review period.
Record the query, the period tested and the affected count on the GRC issue, and have a second analyst re-run it independently.
Classify each affected enrollee by remedy required: claim reprocessing, case reopening, corrected notice, outreach call, or refund.
Freeze the affected-member list as the remediation population of record.
checklist.done: a re-runnable query fixes the affected-enrollee population over the defect's full life with a remedy class per member.

checklist.step: Run the root cause analysis before writing the fix
actions: Facilitate a root cause session with the process owner, the system owner and the staff who worked the failed cases, walking specific failed cases rather than the process diagram.
Distinguish the direct cause (wrong letter template, missed queue) from the underlying cause (staffing model, system configuration, training gap, missing control).
Test the root cause by asking whether fixing it would have prevented each sampled failure.
Record the analysis on the GRC issue — a CAP written without it will not survive CMS validation.
checklist.done: each finding carries a case-tested root cause distinguishing direct from underlying cause.

checklist.step: Comment on the CMS draft report within ten business days
actions: Review each draft condition for factual accuracy against the case records presented during fieldwork.
Draft comments only where the record genuinely contradicts the condition, attaching the case evidence; do not argue classifications without evidence.
Submit the comments through the auditor's stated channel within 10 business days of the draft report and file the submission receipt.
Brief the Compliance Officer on which conditions will stand so CAP drafting starts before the final report lands.
checklist.done: draft-report comments are submitted inside 10 business days with evidence attached and CAP drafting already started.

checklist.step: Draft the corrective action plan to CMS standards
actions: For each final-report condition, write the CAP with numbered actions, a named accountable owner per action, milestone dates, the beneficiary remediation plan from the frozen population, and the metric that will prove effectiveness.
Tie every action to the recorded root cause; strike any action that is retraining alone where the cause is systemic.
Keep milestone dates realistic — a missed CAP milestone is itself reportable — and build the evidence requirement into each milestone.
Have the operational executives confirm resourcing for their actions in writing.
checklist.done: each condition has a CAP with owned, dated, root-cause-tied actions, a beneficiary remediation plan and an effectiveness metric.

checklist.step: Approve and submit the CAP within thirty calendar days
actions: Review the CAP against the final report condition by condition and sign the approval on the GRC issue.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the CAP text, since it concedes the conditions it remediates.
Submit the CAP through the HPMS audit module within 30 calendar days of the final report date and save the submission confirmation.
Log any CMS rejection or revision request the day it arrives and resubmit inside the stated window.
checklist.done: a counsel-cleared, signed CAP is submitted in HPMS inside 30 calendar days with the confirmation saved.

checklist.step: Execute the beneficiary remediation
actions: Work the frozen affected-member list remedy class by remedy class: reprocess the misadjudicated claims with interest where required, reopen the affected appeal cases, and issue corrected notices from the approved templates.
Record the completing transaction identifier against each affected member so completion is provable member by member.
Report weekly completion counts against the population to the Compliance Officer until the list is worked to zero.
Return any unworkable member (deceased, disenrolled, unreachable) to the Compliance Officer for a documented disposition rather than silent removal.
checklist.done: every member on the frozen list shows a completing transaction or a documented disposition, reported weekly to zero.

checklist.step: Implement the systemic fixes
actions: Deliver each CAP action through the owning function: system configuration changes tested and released, letter templates corrected and approved, staffing or queue changes made, procedures rewritten and republished.
Attach the completion evidence the milestone demands — release notes, approved templates, updated procedures, rosters — to the GRC issue at each milestone date.
Refuse milestone closure on a promise; the evidence, not the assertion, closes the milestone.
Flag any milestone at risk to the Compliance Officer at least 10 business days before its date.
checklist.done: every CAP milestone closes on attached evidence by its date or is escalated 10 business days ahead.

checklist.step: Prove effectiveness before declaring the finding remediated
actions: After the fix is live, run the effectiveness metric defined in the CAP over at least one full month of new cases.
Sample 20 post-fix cases and re-perform the originally failed judgement (timeliness, letter content, clinical rationale) against the CMS compliance standard.
Compare the post-fix breach rate to the CAP's effectiveness target and re-open the action if it misses.
File the effectiveness evidence on the GRC issue — this is what the CMS validation audit will re-test.
checklist.done: post-fix sampling and a month of metric data meet the CAP's effectiveness target, filed on the issue.

checklist.step: Prepare for and pass the CMS validation audit
actions: Around 150 days after CAP acceptance, rehearse the validation: re-produce the relevant universes for the post-remediation period and re-run the effectiveness sampling.
Prepare the evidence pack per condition — CAP, milestone evidence, beneficiary remediation completion, effectiveness results — in the order the validation auditor will request it.
Support the validation audit (CMS or its independent auditor) with the same war-room protocol as the original audit.
Log the validation result per condition on the GRC issue the day it is received.
checklist.done: a validation rehearsal was run, the per-condition evidence pack is ready and the validation result is logged per condition.

checklist.step: Track enforcement exposure alongside remediation
actions: Assess each finding for intermediate sanction and civil money penalty exposure under 42 CFR 422.752 and 422.756 and record the assessment on the legal matter.
Manage any enforcement correspondence, ensuring every response is factually consistent with the CAP and the remediation log.
Brief the General Counsel and the board's designated committee on material enforcement exposure quarterly.
Record penalty payments or sanction terms, and their operational conditions, on the matter and the GRC issue.
checklist.done: every finding carries an enforcement exposure assessment and all enforcement correspondence reconciles to the remediation log.

checklist.step: Report remediation status to governance monthly
actions: Report monthly to the Compliance Committee: findings open by source and severity, clock status against every regulatory deadline, milestones at risk, beneficiary remediation completion percentages and validation results.
Show every missed or at-risk clock in red with the recovery plan, never netted into a summary statistic.
Minute the committee's directions and carry them onto the GRC issues.
Escalate any missed regulatory clock to the board's audit committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: a minuted monthly report shows every clock, at-risk milestone and completion rate, with missed clocks escalated to the board.

checklist.step: Close findings and retain the record
actions: Close a finding only on Head of Compliance sign-off, with COO co-sign where enrollees were impacted, after validation passes.

Archive the full finding record — source report, classification, impact analysis, CAP and acceptance, milestone evidence, remediation completion, effectiveness results, validation outcome, sign-offs — indexed by audit and condition number.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm retrieval by condition number returns the complete record in one search.
checklist.done: closed findings carry the required sign-offs and a complete, 10-year-labelled record retrievable by condition number.

testing.step: Build the population of findings from the source documents
actions: Collect every CMS report, notice, warning letter and state exam report received in the period directly from the regulatory correspondence log and counsel's matter list, not from the GRC register.
List every condition in those documents and match each to a GRC issue; an unlogged condition is an automatic fail.
Add all findings open from prior periods to the population.
Sign the population as complete with the source documents referenced.
testing.done: every condition in the period's regulatory correspondence matches a GRC issue, with unlogged conditions failed.

testing.step: Recompute every regulatory clock
actions: For each finding, recompute the deadline from the source letter date: 3 business days for ICAR containment, 10 business days for draft-report comments, 30 calendar days for the CAP, and the stated date for state CAPs.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the logged deadline and to the actual action date, and record days early or late.
Treat any action after the recomputed regulatory deadline as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
Record the clock maths on one timeliness schedule.
testing.done: every finding shows an independently recomputed clock and a measured action date with breaches separately reported.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of ICARs and 100% of findings with beneficiary impact.
Take 10 further findings selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population, minimum 15 findings in total.
Take 100% of findings closed in the period.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every ICAR, every enrollee-impacting finding and every closure.

testing.step: Trace sampled CAP milestones to their evidence
actions: For each sampled finding, open every closed milestone and inspect the attached evidence: release notes, approved templates, published procedures, rosters.
Treat a milestone closed on narrative alone, or with evidence dated after the closure date, as an exception.
Verify the CAP submitted in HPMS matches the CAP approved on the GRC issue word for word.
Capture the HPMS submission confirmation into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled milestone closure rests on dated evidence and the submitted CAP matches the approved text.

testing.step: Re-derive the affected-enrollee population
actions: Re-run the documented impact query for each sampled enrollee-impacting finding and compare the member count to the frozen population of record.
Investigate every member in one result and not the other and classify the cause.
Verify the query period covers the defect's full operating life, not only the audit review period.
Treat an impact population that cannot be re-derived from the documented query as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled impact population re-derives from its documented query over the defect's full life, with differences classified.

testing.step: Verify beneficiary remediation completion member by member
actions: Select 25 members across the sampled remediation lists and trace each to a completing transaction: the reprocessed claim with its adjustment identifier, the reopened case decision, or the corrected notice with its mail date.
Verify interest was paid where the remedy class required it, recomputing one interest amount.
Verify every member removed from the list carries a documented disposition rather than a deletion.
Reconcile the reported completion percentage to the member-level records.
testing.done: sampled members trace to completing transactions, removals carry dispositions and the completion percentage reconciles.

testing.step: Re-perform the effectiveness test on closed findings
actions: For each finding closed in the period, draw 10 post-fix cases independently and re-perform the originally failed judgement against the CMS compliance standard.
Compare your breach rate to the effectiveness result filed on the issue and to the CAP's target.
Treat a closed finding whose independent re-test misses the target as a fail requiring re-opening.
Verify the closure carries the Head of Compliance sign-off and, where enrollees were impacted, the COO co-sign.
testing.done: every closed finding survives an independent post-fix re-test and carries the required closure sign-offs.

testing.step: Verify validation audit results were logged and acted on
actions: For findings that reached CMS validation, compare the validation outcome per condition to the GRC issue status.
Confirm any condition that failed validation was re-opened with a revised CAP inside the window CMS stated.
Confirm the enforcement matter record is consistent with the validation results.
Capture the validation correspondence references into the workpaper.
testing.done: validation outcomes match issue statuses and every failed condition shows a timely re-opened CAP.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per test exception naming the finding, the clock or milestone affected and the impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (finding not logged, clock miscomputed, evidence missing, population not re-derivable, premature closure) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; route any missed regulatory clock to Regulatory Counsel for an enforcement-risk assessment the same week.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the clock compliance rate, the milestone evidence rate and the remediation completion accuracy against the zero-missed-clock threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with a workpaper reference behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who owned no corrective action and drafted no CAP, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any breach to the Compliance Committee and the board's audit committee at their next sittings and file the workpaper by quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, clock and evidence rates and committee reporting dates is filed.
