In-scope systems.value: Marketing materials submitted through the HPMS Marketing Module with material IDs; benefit changes carried in the Bid Submission module; determinations logged in the filing tracker with the material ID or bid reference on each row

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker alerts on every determination row at intake +5 business days if undetermined, plus earliest-use-date reminders to the requesting team and a standing alert 30 days before the first-Monday-in-June bid cut-off for late benefit changes

checklist.step: Run a single intake gate for every product and material change
actions: Require every new or changed benefit, marketing piece, member letter, script, web page, advertisement and sales presentation to enter through the intake queue before any build or print run.
Open a determination row per item recording the requesting team, contracts affected, intended audience, intended first-use date and the artifact itself.
Sweep the marketing asset library and the web publishing calendar weekly for items that bypassed intake, and log each bypass as an exception.
Confirm the requesting team has not scheduled distribution before a determination exists.
checklist.done: every change has a determination row opened before build or distribution, and bypasses are swept weekly.

checklist.step: Classify each item under the 422.2260 definitions
actions: Apply the two-part test from 42 CFR 422.2260: does the content include plan-specific information (benefits, premiums, cost sharing, star ratings) and is the intent to draw attention to the plan or influence enrollment?

Classify each item as marketing (HPMS submission required), communication (no submission, but content rules still apply), or standardized/model material (use CMS text with only permitted variable fields).
Record the classification rationale in one or two sentences on the determination row, quoting the content feature that drove the call.
Route borderline items — items mentioning benefits in passing, retention pieces, TPMO content — to Regulatory Counsel rather than guessing.
checklist.done: every item carries a marketing/communication/model classification with a content-based rationale on its row.

checklist.step: Confirm the jurisdiction call: federal preemption versus state matters
actions: Confirm benefit designs and marketing standards are federally governed under 42 CFR 422.402 preemption and are not filed with state insurance departments through SERFF.
Identify the residual state matters — entity licensure, agent appointment and any state-regulated supplemental products sold alongside the MA plan — and route those to the state filing process.
Record the preemption call on the determination row for any item a state might colorably claim.
Re-check the preemption position when an item bundles MA content with a state-regulated product.
checklist.done: each row records whether the item is federally governed or carries a residual state obligation, with bundled items counsel-checked.

checklist.step: Set the review path for each marketing item
actions: From the procedure's review-path table, mark each marketing item: prospective 45-day CMS review, 5-day File-and-Use with certification where the material type qualifies, or model/standardized material used without alteration beyond permitted fields.
Quote the current 422.2261 basis and any CMS memo relied on for the path onto the determination row.
For model materials, diff the draft against the current CMS model text and confirm only variable fields differ.
Flag every prospective-review item as critical-path for the intended first-use date.
checklist.done: every marketing item carries a review path with its regulatory basis, and model materials are diffed against the CMS text.

checklist.step: Gate benefit changes to the annual bid
actions: For any change touching benefits, premiums or cost sharing, verify it is reflected in the Plan Benefit Package and Bid Pricing Tool for the applicable contract year rather than implemented mid-year.
Hold changes that missed the first-Monday-in-June bid cut-off for the next contract year, and record the hold on the determination row.
Route genuinely permissible mid-year changes (for example CMS-directed corrections) through Regulatory Counsel with the CMS authority cited.
Confirm operational configuration dates match the contract-year effective date, never the request date.
checklist.done: no benefit change is implemented outside an approved bid/PBP or a counsel-cleared CMS-authorized exception.

checklist.step: Apply the content rules before submission
actions: Check each item against the content requirements: required disclaimers and the federal contracting statement, star ratings usage rules, benefit accuracy against the approved PBP, and the TPMO disclaimer where a third-party marketing organization is involved.
Verify translation and alternate-format obligations for the service area's required languages.
Verify prohibited content is absent: absolute superlatives without substantiation, unsubstantiated savings claims, and anything resembling government endorsement.
Record the content check on the determination row with the checker's name.
checklist.done: each item passes a recorded content check covering disclaimers, star ratings, benefit accuracy, TPMO and translation rules.

checklist.step: Submit marketing materials through the HPMS Marketing Module
actions: In HPMS open the Marketing Module, create the material record, and upload the final artifact — obtaining the material ID that must appear on the piece.
For File-and-Use items, complete the certification that the material complies with all applicable standards, and record the submission timestamp that starts the 5-day clock.
For prospective-review items, submit for the 45-day review and record the expected decision date.
Write the material ID and submission timestamp onto the determination row.
checklist.done: every submittable item has an HPMS material ID, a recorded submission timestamp and, where applicable, a completed File-and-Use certification.

checklist.step: Compute and publish the earliest-use date per item
actions: Compute the earliest-use date: submission date + 5 calendar days for File-and-Use, the CMS approval date for prospective review, the contract-year start for bid-gated changes, and immediate for pure communications that passed the content check.
Write the earliest-use date on the determination row and notify the requesting team and the print/mail and digital publishing owners.
For the ANOC, verify the mailing plan lands delivery by 30 September per 42 CFR 422.111.
Diarise a check on the first-use date to confirm the gate held.
checklist.done: every item carries a computed earliest-use date, notified to every distribution owner, with ANOC delivery planned by 30 September.

checklist.step: Arm the distribution gate in the publishing channels
actions: Configure the marketing automation platform and web CMS so an asset cannot be scheduled before the earliest-use date recorded on its determination row.
Instruct print and mail vendors in writing that no job releases without the material ID and earliest-use date on the work order.
Hold sales event materials and agent-facing presentations to the same gate through the distribution portal.
Spot-check five scheduled campaigns each month against their determination rows.
checklist.done: no channel can release an asset before its earliest-use date, vendors hold the same rule in writing, and spot-checks run monthly.

checklist.step: Track CMS dispositions and withdraw disapproved materials
actions: Check the HPMS Marketing Module for review dispositions on submitted items at least twice weekly and record each disposition on the determination row.
On a disapproval or required correction, stop distribution the same business day: pull the asset from every channel, halt pending print and mail jobs, and notify vendors in writing.
Correct and resubmit the material, or retire it, and record both actions with dates.
File the CMS disposition correspondence in the evidence pack — the regulation requires disapproved material to be withdrawn or corrected.
checklist.done: every disposition is recorded within two business days and disapproved materials show a same-day distribution stop with vendor notices.

checklist.step: Oversee TPMO and agent-created materials
actions: Require every third-party marketing organization and agent-created piece referencing the plans to enter the same intake gate before use, per the TPMO oversight terms in the distribution agreements.
Verify TPMO materials carry the required TPMO disclaimer and, where they are marketing, an HPMS material ID under the plan's or the TPMO's submission.
Sweep agent social media and lead-generation sites quarterly for unapproved plan references and route findings to intake as exceptions.
Log oversight results by agency for the conduct-metric pack.
checklist.done: TPMO and agent materials pass the same gate, carry the required disclaimer and IDs, and a quarterly sweep feeds exceptions to intake.

checklist.step: Support every 'no submission required' call in writing
actions: Review each communication and model-material classification where the item touches benefits, cost sharing or enrollment, re-reading the 422.2260 definitions rather than relying on precedent alone.
Confirm or overturn the call in writing on the determination row; overturned items go back for HPMS submission before use.
Never allow a row to close on 'not marketing' without a stated reason tied to the definition.
Stamp confirmed rows with counsel name and date.
checklist.done: every no-submission call on a benefit-touching item carries a dated counsel confirmation with a definition-based reason.

checklist.step: Escalate when the intended launch cannot survive the review clock
actions: Compare each item's earliest-use date to the requesting team's launch date as soon as the review path is set.

Where the launch date is unreachable, escalate in writing to the Marketing Manager and the Head of Compliance within one business day with the options: move the launch, switch to a qualifying File-and-Use format, or use an existing approved material.
Record the decision and its owner on the determination row — distributing before the earliest-use date is never one of the options.
Track escalation frequency by requesting team to expose chronic late intake.
checklist.done: every unreachable launch date has a written, owned decision that keeps distribution behind the earliest-use date.

checklist.step: Reconcile circulation to the determination log monthly
actions: Pull the month's distributed-asset list from the marketing automation platform, the web CMS and the print/mail vendor manifests.
Match every distributed asset to a determination row and an earliest-use date on or before its first distribution.
Log any unmatched or premature asset as an exception the same day and trigger the withdrawal drill where required.
Report the reconciliation result in the monthly compliance dashboard.
checklist.done: every distributed asset in the month matches a determination row with a compliant earliest-use date, or is an exception in remediation.

checklist.step: Retain the determination evidence for ten years
actions: Archive each determination row with its artifact version, classification rationale, HPMS material ID and confirmation, certification or approval, counsel sign-offs and gate-release notes, indexed by material ID and contract year.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Confirm a search by material ID returns the full determination record in one query.
Record the archive reference on the closed row.
checklist.done: every closed determination is archived under a 10-year label and retrievable by material ID in one search.

testing.step: Build the population of changes and distributed materials
actions: Pull the quarter's intake log, the marketing automation and web CMS distribution lists, the print/mail vendor manifests and the HPMS Marketing Module material list for the same period.
Build the population from the distribution side — what actually reached members and prospects — so items that bypassed intake cannot escape the test.
Reconcile the four sources against each other and list assets appearing in circulation but not in the intake log.
Sign the population as complete with source extract dates.
testing.done: a circulation-based population reconciled across four sources exists, with intake bypasses listed.

testing.step: Reconcile circulated marketing items to HPMS material IDs
actions: For every circulated item classified as marketing, verify a material ID exists in the HPMS Marketing Module and appears on the artifact itself.
List any marketing item in circulation with no HPMS record as an automatic fail.
Verify the artifact version in circulation matches the version submitted to HPMS, not a later edit.
Capture the HPMS material records into the workpaper.
testing.done: every circulated marketing item traces to an HPMS material ID and the circulated version matches the submitted version.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of items flagged as exceptions or bypasses, 100% of disapproved or corrected materials, and 100% of AEP enrollment materials in the fourth-quarter test.
Take 25 further items selected at random with a recorded seed across marketing, communication and model classifications.
Include at least five 'no submission required' calls and at least three TPMO or agent-created pieces.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all exceptions, disapprovals, AEP materials, no-submission calls and TPMO pieces.

testing.step: Re-perform the marketing-versus-communication classification
actions: Read each sampled artifact and reach your own classification under the 42 CFR 422.2260 content-and-intent test before reading the determination row.
Compare to the recorded classification; a right call with a rationale that does not cite the content feature is a documentation exception.
For sampled model materials, diff the circulated artifact against the current CMS model text and flag any change beyond permitted variable fields.
Capture the definition text and your assessment into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled item has an independent classification compared to the recorded call, with model-text diffs attached.

testing.step: Recompute the earliest-use date and test the gate
actions: Recompute each sampled item's earliest-use date from the source facts: HPMS submission timestamp + 5 calendar days for File-and-Use, the CMS approval date for prospective review, the contract-year start for bid-gated changes.
Compare the first actual distribution date from the channel logs and vendor manifests to the recomputed earliest-use date.
Treat any distribution before the recomputed date as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
Record the day-count maths on one schedule.
testing.done: every sampled item shows a recomputed earliest-use date and a measured first-distribution date with breaches separately reported.

testing.step: Verify File-and-Use certifications and prospective approvals
actions: For sampled File-and-Use items, open the HPMS record and confirm the certification was completed at submission by an authorised submitter.
For sampled prospective-review items, confirm the CMS approval disposition pre-dates first distribution.
Confirm the disposition on the determination row matches the HPMS record.
Capture the HPMS disposition screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled certifications and approvals are verified in HPMS and match the determination rows.

testing.step: Test the disapproval withdrawal drill end to end
actions: For every disapproved or correction-required material in the period, read the CMS notification date and trace the same-day distribution stop: channel takedown logs, halted print jobs, vendor notices.
Verify the corrected material was resubmitted and re-dispositioned before any re-use.
Search the current channels for the disapproved version to confirm it is genuinely out of circulation.
Treat a disapproved version still reachable in any channel as a fail.
testing.done: every disapproved material shows a traced same-day stop, a compliant resubmission and no residual circulation.

testing.step: Test the no-submission calls and counsel sign-offs
actions: For each sampled 'no submission required' call, verify a dated Regulatory Counsel confirmation exists with a definition-based reason.
Re-read the artifact against 422.2260 and challenge any communication classification on an item that names benefits, cost sharing or star ratings.
Verify benefit-touching items with no counsel confirmation are logged as procedure exceptions.
Record your challenge outcomes in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled no-submission call carries a dated counsel confirmation and survives an independent definition challenge.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception naming the material ID or item, the contracts affected and what failed.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list (intake bypass, misclassification, day-count error, gate not armed, vendor released early, withdrawal incomplete) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; for any premature or unsubmitted marketing use, open a disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel for the CMS Account Manager.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where required, a disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the gate compliance rate, the classification accuracy rate and the withdrawal completion rate against the zero-premature-distribution threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective) with a workpaper reference behind each statement.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no determination and submitted no material, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper by quarter.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, gate and classification rates and a committee reporting date is filed.
